titles: 1-14 KINGDOM OF THE UNIVERSE BELONG TO ALLAH AND LOWER HEAVEN IS DECORATED WITH THE LAMPS (STARS) AND CONVERSATION BETWEEN THE DWELLERS OF HELL AND HER GUARDS
15-30 NO ONE CAN HELP YOU AGAINST ALLAH AND NO ONE CAN PROVIDE YOU SUSTENANCE BESIDES ALLAH AND NO ONE CAN SAVE YOU FROM THE PUNISHMENT OF ALLAH

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the very first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is one of the earliest Surahs to be revealed at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
This surah focuses on awakening human awareness of Allah SWT’s power, purpose, and judgment. It begins by showing that the universe is perfectly created, and governed solely by Allah SWT, leaving no flaw or weakness.
Allah SWT owns life and death → therefore humans will be tested → therefore accountability is real.
Man is reminded that he was not created without purpose but sent to be tested through his deeds. The surah then warns of the terrible end awaiting disbelievers in the Hereafter. People are warned that the Day of Judgment is inevitable, even if its timing is unknown; when it arrives, the disbelievers who mocked the warning will be struck with horror.
Next, the Surah draws attention to everyday signs of Allah SWT’s power — the stability of the earth, the flight of birds, the control of sustenance, and protection from calamity — urging reflection instead of heedlessness.
Finally, the Surah ends with a powerful question that humbles human pride: What if the water you depend on were to vanish into the ground, who could bring it back except Allah SWT ? The message throughout is clear — recognize the Creator’s power, live with awareness and righteousness, and prepare for the life to come.
ONE SHOULD READ THIS SURAH BEFORE GOING TO SLEEP.

sections.title: 1-14 KINGDOM OF THE UNIVERSE BELONG TO ALLAH AND LOWER HEAVEN IS DECORATED WITH THE LAMPS (STARS) AND CONVERSATION BETWEEN THE DWELLERS OF HELL AND HER GUARDS

arabic_lines: تَبٰرَكَ الَّذِىۡ بِيَدِهِ الۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلٰى كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ قَدِيۡرُۙ

translation.text: Blessed is the One in Whose Hands rests all authority. And He is Most Capable of everything.

commentary.text: All MULK that is power and authority are with Allah SWT. We must remember that in all aspects of our life and not succumb to human desires or authority.
Name of Ayat.

translation.text: ˹He is the One˺ Who created death and life in order to test which of you is best in deeds. And He is the Almighty, All-Forgiving.

commentary.text: Allah SWT created life and death to test human beings and reveal who among them performs the best deeds. It reminds us that both life and death are under Allah SWT’s control alone — no one else can give or take life.

Our existence is not meaningless; it is a deliberate test. Life is the time given for action, and death marks the end of that opportunity. Through this test, every person shows what kind of choices they make — good or evil — and Allah SWT alone will judge their deeds by His standard, not by human opinion.

The Ayat concludes by describing Allah as “Al-ʿAzīz, Al-Ghafūr” — the Almighty, the Most Forgiving. This means that although Allah SWT has full power to punish wrongdoers and no one can escape His judgment, He is also Merciful and Forgiving to those who repent and strive to do good. Thus, the Ayat balances fear and hope: it calls believers to act righteously out of awareness of accountability while trusting in Allah SWT’s mercy and forgiveness.
In life we are being tested as to our belief in Allah SWT (IMAN) + our action (GOOD DEEDS). Do we succumb to our worldly desires or live life as prescribed by Allah.

Lesson: Right now, no accounting on TEST. Hereafter no TEST only accounting. Allah SWT did not create us for worldly work, life, enjoyment rather for His Worship and obedience. So even when we are doing our work, household chores, driving, walking etc do zikr and remember and be grateful to Allah SWT.

translation.text: ˹He is the One˺ Who created seven heavens, one above the other. You will never see any imperfection in the creation of the Most Compassionate. So look again: do you see any flaws?

commentary.text: Ayat e Mutashabihat. The perfection and harmony of Allah SWT’s creation is being described here. Allah SWT declares that He is the One who created the seven heavens, one above the other, meaning they are layered or arranged in levels, each distinct and orderly. Scholars have two views on whether these heavens are directly connected or separated by space; the stronger opinion, supported by the Prophet’s Night Journey (Isrā’), is that they are separate realms, one above another.

Allah SWT then challenges human perception, saying: “You can see no flaw in the creation of the Most Merciful.” This means the universe is flawless—there is no disorder, inconsistency, or imperfection in Allah SWT’s design. Everything is balanced, precise, and purposeful. Allah SWT invites man to look again at the sky and examine it carefully: “Do you see any flaws?”—that is, any cracks, tears, or defects. The answer is no.

Allah SWT calls human beings to reflect deeply on the order, beauty, and perfection of creation, so they may recognize His power and wisdom. The harmony of the heavens is a sign that the Creator’s work is without error, and that everything in existence points to His greatness and majesty.

translation.text: Then look again and again—your sight will return frustrated and weary.

commentary.text: Keep looking and you will find no fault or flaw in Allah SWT’s creation.

translation.text: And indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with ˹stars like˺ lamps and made them ˹as missiles˺ for stoning ˹eavesdropping˺ devils, for whom We have also prepared the torment of the Blaze.

commentary.text: The first sky is adorned with stars as light and also as missiles for the jinn who ease drop as to the orders of what the angles are being commanded to carry out.

translation.text: Those who disbelieve in their Lord will suffer the punishment of Hell. What an evil destination!
They will hear it drawing in its breath when they are thrown in. It blazes forth,

commentary.text: When they are cast into Hell, they will hear its Shahiq (inhaling), and the sound of shouting/screaming while it is simmering. It will boil them just as a small number of seeds are boiled in a lot of water.

translation.text: Almost bursting with rage. Its keepers will ask every group that is thrown in, ‘Did no one come to warn you?’

commentary.text: This Ayat describes Hell raging fiercely, almost bursting with anger. Each time a group of disbelievers is thrown into it, the angels guarding Hell will ask, “Did no messenger come to you?” The question is meant to make them realize that they were clearly warned by Allah SWTs prophets but chose to reject the truth. It shows that Allah SWT never punishes anyone without sending guidance first, and that those who ignored the warnings and followed their desires will face the consequences of their own choices.

translation.text: They will reply, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we did not believe him. We said, “God has revealed nothing: you are greatly misguided”.
And so they will confess their sins. So away with the residents of the Blaze!

commentary.text: The people will not be destroyed until they themselves confess their guilt. They will then have passed through the fire of Judgement and will now be in the fire of Punishment. The Reality will not only now be clear to them, but after the questionings of the angels they cannot even pretend to make any excuses. They will freely confess, but that is not repentance, for repentance implies amendment, and the time for repentance and amendment will have long been past.

The word dhanb (sin) has been used in the singular. It means that the real sin because of which they became worthy of Hell was to belie the Messengers and refuse to obey them. All other sins are its consequences.
Lesson: Use your faculties to obey Allah SWT and reflect upon his universe to increase your faith. Don’t blindly and dumbly follow the herd like cattle.
REPENT OFTEN IN THIS WORLD.

translation.text: Surely forgiveness and a mighty reward await those who fear Allah without seeing Him.

commentary.text: Those who fear Allah SWT in private, avoiding sin and doing good, will receive forgiveness and a great reward. Ibn Kathīr explains that such people act sincerely for Allah SWT alone, not for show. He links this to the hadith about the seven people shaded by Allah SWT on Judgment Day—like the man who resists temptation saying, “I fear Allah,” and the one who gives charity secretly. The Ayat reminds us that Allah SWT knows every hidden thought, so true faith is shown through sincerity and obedience when no one else is watching.

translation.text: Whether you speak secretly or openly—He surely knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed about the idolaters who used to slander the Messenger of Allah SWT. Angel Gabriel informed the Prophet (PBUH) about the things with which they slandered him. Some of them used to say to others: ‘Lower your voices lest Muhammad’s Allah hears you.”

translation.text: Would He not know, He Who has created, when He is All-Subtle, All-Aware?

commentary.text: This is the argument for what has been said in the preceding Ayats. That is, how is it possible that the Creator should be unaware of His creation? The creation may remain unaware of itself, but the Creator cannot be unaware of it. He has made every vein of your body, every fiber of your heart and brain. You breathe because He enables you to breathe, your limb’s function because He enables them to function, how then can anything of yours remain hidden from Him.
His knowledge is further characterized as understanding the finest mysteries and being well-acquainted with them (LATIF is aware of something that is discreet AND KHABIR is what we publize).

translation.text: He it is Who made the earth subservient to you. So traverse in its tracks and partake of the sustenance He has provided. To Him will you be resurrected.

commentary.text: Allah SWT has made the earth easy and manageable for human beings, enabling them to live, travel, and benefit from it. However, it is imperative to keep in mind that All provision comes from Allah SWT—human effort only succeeds by His will.

Ibn Kathīr explains that this teaches balance between effort and trust (tawakkul). The Prophet (PBUH) said, “If you trust in Allah SWT as you should, He will provide for you as He provides for the birds; they leave in the morning hungry and return full in the evening.” This shows that believers must strive for their needs while relying completely on Allah SWT’s decree.

translation.text: Are you sure that He who is in Heaven will not send a whirlwind to pelt you with stones? You will come to know what My warning means.
And certainly those before them denied ˹as well˺, then how severe was My response!
Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Compassionate. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.

commentary.text: Allah SWT invites us to reflect upon His everyday miracles — for example the flight of birds. Allah SWT says: “Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and closing their wings, with none holding them except the Most Merciful? Indeed, He oversees everything.”

It reminds us that every bird flies only through Allah SWT’s power and mercy. He is the One who gave each bird its unique body, wings, and balance; taught it how to fly; and subjected the air to laws that allow even heavier-than-air bodies to soar. Every moment a bird remains in flight, it does so under Allah SWT’s protection.

The Ayat concludes, “He is All-Seeing of everything,” meaning Allah SWT’s care and control extend beyond the birds to all of creation. Every creature lives, moves, and survives only because of His constant guardianship and wisdom.

translation.text: Or who is it that will provide for you if He withholds His provision? In fact, they persist in arrogance and aversion ˹to the truth˺.

commentary.text: If Allah SWT decides to withhold provision you can do nothing, yet you daringly persist in arrogance and deny in disobedience.
Lesson: Allah SWT specifically mentions withholding of provision. Reflect. What am I doing and what is my position.

translation.text: Who is ˹rightly˺ guided: the one who crawls facedown or the one who walks upright on the Straight Path?

commentary.text: A powerful parable contrasts the believer and the disbeliever. Allah SWT asks: “Is he who walks fallen on his face more rightly guided, or he who walks upright on a straight path?”

The disbeliever is likened to a person walking on his face — unable to see clearly, stumbling without direction or purpose. This image reflects his spiritual state: lost, confused, and blind to guidance. In contrast, the believer walks upright on a straight path — clear in vision, firm in purpose, and guided by truth. His path is straight, and his heart is upright, aligned with divine guidance.
Ibn Kathīr explains that this likeness applies both in this world and in the Hereafter.
Faith gives clarity, direction, and dignity, while disbelief leads only to confusion, humiliation, and ruin.

Lesson: Don’t live blindly by base/lowly human instincts to eat, sleep, etc. Like animals.  Rise above and stand tall on the path of faith. Have a higher ideal in life not just to live. Realize your worth.

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “He is the One Who brought you into being and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT reminds us that He has granted us intellect, sight, and hearing not for blind imitation but for reflection and guidance. Allah SWT endowed humans with reason to distinguish truth from falsehood (unlike cattle). These faculties were given so they could recognize divine signs, understand revelation, and choose the right path.
Ibn Kathīr and other commentators explain that to use these gifts merely to follow tradition or desire is ingratitude toward Allah SWT’s blessings.
Thus, hearing, sight, and reason are sacred trusts, meant to lead to faith and gratitude—not to blind imitation or disbelief.

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Consider this: whether Allah causes me and those with me to die or shows us mercy, who will save the disbelievers from a painful punishment?”

commentary.text: This statement was directed to the idolaters of Makkah, who mocked the Prophet (PBUH) and wished for his destruction. Allah SWT tells them that their salvation does not depend on what happens to others — every person is responsible for their own belief and deeds.

Ibn Kathīr explains that this Ayat exposes the false security of the disbelievers. They took comfort in mocking the Prophet (PBUH) and denying his message, thinking his death or downfall would somehow spare them from punishment. But Allah SWT clarifies that their only protection lies in repentance and submission, not in hoping for harm to come to the righteous.

translation.text: Say, “He is the Most Compassionate—in Him ˹alone˺ we believe, and in Him ˹alone˺ we trust. You will soon know who is clearly astray.”

commentary.text: IMAN + TAWAQUL.

That is, we have believed in God, and you are denying Him; we have put our trust in Him, and you have put your trust in yourself, your own resources and false deities besides Allah; therefore, only we deserve to be shown mercy by Allah, not you.

translation.text: Say to them: “Did you even consider: if all the water that you have (in the wells) were to sink down into the depths of the earth, who will produce for you clear, flowing water?”

commentary.text: This final Ayat delivers a striking and humbling reminder of Allah SWT’s absolute power and humanity’s total dependence on Him.

The word غَوْرًا (ghā’iran) means water that disappears deep underground, so that it cannot be reached—no matter how much effort, strength, or technology humans apply. Allah SWT challenges mankind to reflect: if He were to cause all water to vanish into the depths of the earth, who could restore it?

Ibn Kathīr explains that “flowing water” (مَاءً مَعِينًا) refers to fresh, springing, running water that sustains life. Only Allah SWT causes it to gush forth, flow across the earth, and reach people in just the right amounts—sometimes abundant, sometimes scarce—according to His wisdom. This constant, balanced supply is purely a gift of His mercy and grace. None of the false gods or worldly powers can create or restore even a single drop of water.

Thus, this closing Ayah beautifully encapsulates the message of the entire surah: Allah is the Creator, Sustainer, and Controller of all existence. Every blessing—from the air we breathe to the water we drink—flows from Him alone. So we must reflect and give thanks after recognizing that all belongs to Allah SWT, the Lord and Sustainer of every living thing

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of this Surah is from Ayat 1 Al Qalam. NUN is also the name for a fish in Ayat 48.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This too is one of the earliest surahs to be revealed at Makkah, but its subject matter shows that it was sent down at the time when opposition to the Holy Prophet (upon whom be peace) had grown very harsh and tyrannical.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Qalam (The Pen) is one of the earliest Makki revelations, revealed when opposition to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) had become harsh. The Surah has three main themes: refuting the objections of the disbelievers, warning them through examples and admonitions, and urging the Prophet (PBUH) to remain patient and steadfast.
It begins by assuring the Prophet (PBUH) that he is not mad, as accused by his opponents, and the Quran itself testify to his truth and character. It then describes the corrupt character of a known opponent, contrasting it with the Prophet’s noble conduct.
The parable of the garden owners warns the Quraysh that arrogance and ingratitude for divine blessings lead to destruction, both in this world and the Hereafter. The disbelievers are reminded that the righteous and the sinful cannot have the same fate, and that their temporary ease is not a sign of divine approval. Finally, the Prophet (PBUH) is instructed to endure with patience, like other prophets before him, especially avoiding the haste shown by Prophet Yunus/ Jonah, and to trust in Allah’s ultimate judgment.

sections.title: 1-16 ALLAH HAS DECLARED MUHAMMAD TO BE OF THE HIGHEST MORAL CHARACTER AND DO NOT YIELD ANY DISBELIEVING OATH MONGER, SLANDERER AND WICKED PERSON

translation.text: Nũn. By the pen and what everyone writes!
By the grace of your Lord, you ˹O Prophet˺ are not insane.

commentary.text: Allah SWT mentions the letter Nun, like the letters Sad and Qaf found in other Surahs. These are special letters whose meanings are known only to Allah SWT.

Then Allah SWT swears/takes an oath by the Pen, -- reminding us of the great gift of writing, through which humans learn and share knowledge, as also mentioned in Surah Al-‘Alaq – that the Prophet (PBUH) is not mad.

The phrase “and what everyone writes” means what people or angels record—either human writings or the deeds of people written by angels. Some scholars say it refers to the first Pen Allah SWT created, which wrote everything that would happen until the end of time.
Lesson: If you have a ability to write then write something useful.

translation.text: You will certainly have a never-ending reward.
And you are truly ˹a man˺ of outstanding character.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is praising the character of the Prophet (PBUH). Ayesha (May Allah be pleased with her) said the Quran was the character of the Prophet (PBUH). Prophet had the best manners, patience, tolerance and forgiveness. Best physical characteristics and inner characteristics that relate to how you make a person feel.
A servant of the Prophet (PBUH) who worked with him for 10 years said the Prophet (PBUH) never said a bad word to him in all that time.

translation.text: Soon you and the pagans will see,

commentary.text: Allah SWT is consoling the Prophet (PBUH) gently. The reward for the Prophet is never-ending and great. Allah SWT praises the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for his noble character. It carries two meanings: first, that his strong and noble character enabled him to bear hardships while guiding people to the truth; and second, that his high morals themselves prove the falsehood of those who called him mad—because true moral perfection and madness cannot exist together.

The people of Makkah knew his honesty, patience, mercy, and integrity, making such accusations baseless. His wife Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) beautifully described him by saying, “His character was the Qur’an”—meaning he lived the Qur’an’s teachings completely. He never struck anyone, never sought revenge for personal reasons, and always chose ease unless it led to sin. Those who served him, like Anas ibn Malik, testified that he was never harsh or critical. His life was the living example of perfect manners and divine guidance.

translation.text: which of you is mad.
Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.

commentary.text: These above seven Ayats are the second Wahi/revelation sent to the Prophet (PBUH)

translation.text: So do not give in to the deniers.

commentary.text: Prohibition of giving into the Pressure of the Disbelievers and Their Suggestions, and that They like to meet in the Middle of the Path. The mushriqeen of Mecca wanted the Prophet (PBUH) to acknowledge the idols and make some religious compromise. Then they would accept Islam. Allah SWT says DO NOT!! Do not change the truth to make it more acceptable or palatable to some.

translation.text: They wish you would compromise so they would yield ˹to you˺.

commentary.text: That is, if you became inclined to effect some changes in your faith to suit these people, they too would affect a compromise with you.
Lesson: Falsehood always is eager and wanting to compromise. However, those on the truth hold firmly to their principles. Don’t get caught up in pleasing people.

translation.text: And do not obey the despicable, vain oath-taker,

commentary.text: And do not obey every Hallaf (one who swears much) Mahin (liar or worthless person). This is because the liar, due to his weakness of character uses false oaths using Allah's Names, and he uses them (false oaths) all the time and out of place (i.e., unnecessarily). Someone who constantly swears that he is sincere and a well-wisher towards you.

translation.text: slanderer, gossip-monger,

commentary.text: The word هَمَّازٍ (Hammaz) means someone who mocks, criticizes, or slanders others. A person who habitually speaks ill of others. Someone who spreads gossip to create conflict and harm relationships. Islam strongly condemns this behavior.

Hadith: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) once passed by two graves and said that the people in them were being punished—not for great sins in people’s eyes, but for serious ones in Allah SWT’s sight: one for being careless about purity after urination, and the other for spreading gossip. These teachings show that backbiting, gossip, and causing discord among people are grave sins that destroy trust and community harmony.

translation.text: withholder of good, transgressor, evildoer
translation.ref_as_written: printed (68:11); text is 68:12 (withholder of good, transgressor)

commentary.text: Khayr in Arabic is used both for wealth and for good. If it is taken in the meaning of wealth, the meaning would be that he is miserly and stingy. And if khayr is taken in the meaning of goodness and virtue, it would mean that he creates a hindrance in every good work as well as that he is very active in hindering the people from accepting Islam.
A person greedy in eating and drinking and is also ill-mannered, quarrelsome and cruel at the same time.

translation.text: the coarse-grained, and above all mean and ignoble

commentary.text: A person who is notorious among the people for his evildoing.

The views of the commentators about the person who has been described in these above Ayats are different. Majority say it was WALID BIN MUGHIRAH; others say it was Aswad bin Abdi Yaghuth, and some other people have pointed to some other persons.

But the Quran has only described his attributes without naming him. This shows that in Makkah the man concerned was so notorious for his such qualities that there was no need to name him. Hearing his description every person could understand who was being referred to.

translation.text: Now, ˹simply˺ because he has been blessed with ˹abundant˺ wealth and children,

commentary.text: This Ayat may relate to the preceding theme as well as with the following Ayat. In the first case, it would mean: Do not yield to the influence of such a person just because he has plenty of wealth and children. In the second: He has become proud because he possesses abundance of wealth and children; so when Our revelations are recited to him, he says: These are tales of ancient times.
Lesson: Be careful of who you obey or follow. Understand that worldly wealth in no criteria. ALLAH SWT GAVE TO EVEN A PERSON WHOM HE DETESTED. Iman + Good Deeds is what we will be judged by.

translation.text: whenever Our revelations are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”

commentary.text: When Allah SWT’s revelations are recited to him, he arrogantly says, “These are ancient fables!”—meaning he rejects the truth, claiming the Quran is just old stories made up by earlier people. This shows his pride and disbelief, as he refuses to accept divine guidance even after being blessed with wealth and children. His mockery reflects his ingratitude and blindness to Allah SWT’s message.

translation.text: We will soon mark his snout.

commentary.text: This man was thought to be a man of high prestige, his nose has been called a snout and branding him on the snout means disgracing him. That is, Allah SWT shall disgrace him in the world and in the Hereafter to the point that his mark of disgrace will become indelible.
His matter will be made so clear and evident that all will know him and he will not be hidden from them, just as the branding mark on the snouts (of animals).

sections.title: 17-33 WHAT HAPPENED TO THE ARROGANT STINGY OWNERS OF A GARDEN WHO DID NOT WANT TO PAY CHARITY?

arabic_lines: اِنَّا بَلَوۡنٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَاۤ اَصۡحٰبَ الۡجَـنَّةِ ۚ اِذۡ اَقۡسَمُوۡا لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِيۡ

commentary.text: Also see Surah Kahf Ayat 32-44
The parable of the owners of two gardens has been cited for teaching a lesson

This is a parable that Allah SWT made regarding the behavior of the Quraysh disbelievers despite the favor of sending of Muhammad (PBUH) to them. They met him with denial, rejection and opposition. Therefore, Allah SWT says, He tested them just as He tested the People of the Garden who vowed between themselves during the night that they would pluck the fruit of the garden in the morning so that poor and the beggars would not know what they were doing. In this way they would be able to keep its fruit for themselves and not give any of it in charity.

translation.text: leaving no thought for Allah’s Will.

commentary.text: They were so sure and confident of their power and authority that they swore they would definitely pluck the fruit of their garden next morning, without feeling any need to say: “We shall do so if Allah so willed.”

translation.text: Thereupon a calamity from your Lord passed over it while they were asleep,
so it was reduced to ashes.

commentary.text: Some heavenly destruction was afflicted upon them.

translation.text: Then by daybreak they called out to each other,
˹saying,˺ “Go early to your harvest, if you want to pick ˹all˺ the fruit.”
“Do not let any poor person enter your garden today.”
And they proceeded early, totally fixated on their purpose.

commentary.text: And they went in the morning with strength and power. meaning, they thought they had power to do what they claimed and what they desired.

Lesson: This is the nature of man – full of pride, arrogance, and certainty – ready to conquer the world yet not knowing that infact there is a calamity awaiting like cancer in the body. This is the characteristics of those who are away from Iman and do not believe in the Hereafter. They wanted to deprive others and they were deprived.

translation.text: But when they saw the garden, they said, ‘We must have lost our way!

commentary.text: When they arrived at the garden it was in the condition which Allah SWT had changed from luster, brilliance and abundance of fruit, to being black, gloomy and void of any benefit. They believed that they had been mistaken in the path they took in walking to it. Until realized with certainty that it was the correct path (garden).

translation.text: In fact, we have been deprived ˹of our livelihood˺.”

commentary.text: They realized there was no harvest left only destruction and barren land.

arabic_lines: قَالَ اَوۡسَطُهُمۡ اَلَمۡ اَقُلۡ لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُوۡنَ

commentary.text: When they were saying with certainty that: “we shall surely pluck the fruit of our garden tomorrow, “this person had warned them at that time, saying: Have you forgotten God? Why don’t you say: If Allah so wills? But they did not listen to him. Then, while they were making up their mind not to give away anything to the needy, he again advised them to remember Allah SWT and to desist from their evil intention, but they persisted in what they had resolved.

translation.text: They replied, “Glory be to our Lord! We have truly been wrongdoers.”

commentary.text: They became obedient and were remorseful.

sections.title: 34-43 ALLAH IS NOT GOING TO TREAT THE MUSLIMS AS HE WILL TREAT THE GUILTY WHY DISBELIEVERS DO NOT UNDERSTAND THIS?

translation.text: That is the ˹way of Our˺ punishment ˹in this world˺. But the punishment of the Hereafter is certainly far worse, if only they knew.

commentary.text: Moral Lesson of this Story: Such is the punishment of whoever opposes the command of Allah SWT, is stingy with what Allah SWT has given him and, withholds the right of the poor and needy, and responds to Allah SWT's blessings with ungratefulness (or disbelief). This is the punishment of this life but truly, the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they but knew.
Lesson: In this life one can repent and make amends but, in the Hereafter, there is no room for anything but eternal pain and suffering. Every Monday and Thursday fast and seek repentance.

translation.text: Indeed, the righteous will have the Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.

commentary.text: TAQWA = SUCCESS

translation.text: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?

commentary.text: It is illogical and unjust to believe Allah SWT would treat good and evil people alike. A just Creator must distinguish between those who obey His commands and those who reject them. The disbelievers saw believers struggling while they enjoyed comfort. They assumed worldly ease meant divine approval. In truth, Allah SWT’s justice ensures that the obedient will be rewarded, and the guilty will face punishment.
Lesson: MUSLIM AND MUJRIM (CRIMINAL) ARE NOT THE SAME. DEATH IS THE LEVELER.

translation.text: Or do you have a scripture, in which you read

commentary.text: Have you read this in any Book that the guilty will not be punished after death?

translation.text: Or do they have associate-gods ˹supporting this claim˺? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods, if what they say is true.
˹Beware of˺ the Day the Shin ˹of Allah˺ will be bared, and the wicked will be asked to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so,

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgement, when people will face great fear and turmoil. the reality of divine power and truth will become clear, and people will be called to bow before Allah SWT — but only the sincere believers will be able to do so. Those who used to pray for show or out of habit, without true faith, will find themselves unable to bow, as their backs will become stiff and unbending.
This powerful scene shows the difference between genuine faith and hypocrisy, reminding us that only sincere worship done for Allah SWT’s sake will matter on that Day.

translation.text: with eyes downcast, totally covered with disgrace. For they were ˹always˺ called to prostrate ˹in the world˺ when they were fully capable ˹but they chose not to˺.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgment, Allah SWT will reveal those who truly worshiped Him and those who only pretended or refused. Everyone will be commanded to prostrate, but only the sincere believers will be able to do so.

The disbelievers and hypocrites—who were once healthy and able to bow in this life but chose arrogance instead—will find themselves unable to bend, their backs stiff and straight. Their eyes will be cast down in shame, and humiliation will cover them as a just punishment for their pride and disbelief.

This powerful image shows that those who ignored Allah SWT’s call in ease will lose the ability to respond when it matters most. Their physical inability will mirror their spiritual hardness in the world.

Lesson: Our purpose in life is to pray and worship Allah SWT. Prostrate now and often. Pray in a standing position as much as you can and put your head on the ground in sujood. All prostrations in this world are a dress rehearsal or practice for when we stand before Allah SWT and then prostrate before Him, in sha Allah.

sections.title: 44-52 THOSE WHO DO NOT BELIEVE IN ALLAH'S REVELATIONS ARE LED STEP BY STEP TOWARDS DESTRUCTION

translation.text: So leave to Me ˹O Prophet˺ those who reject this message. We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend.

commentary.text: According to Ibn Kathir, Allah SWT tells the Prophet (PBUH) not to concern himself with those who deny the Quran; Allah SWT Himself will deal with them.

He warns that He will punish them gradually, from directions they do not perceive. The disbelievers think that their wealth, health, and worldly success are signs of divine favor, but these are testament to lead them deeper into heedlessness and sin. Allah SWT says elsewhere: “We will seize them gradually from directions they do not know” (68:44), and “Do they think that in giving them wealth and children We hasten good for them? Nay, they perceive not.” (23:55–56).

The deeper meaning, as the scholars explain, is that Allah SWT sometimes allows a person who rejects the truth to prosper outwardly, so that he becomes deluded by his comfort and assumes his actions are right. This false sense of security blinds him to his rebellion and arrogance until the moment of sudden punishment arrives. Thus, what seems like blessing is a slow path to ruin — a form of divine justice in which Allah SWT’s lets the proud become trapped by their own deception.

IN ESSENCE, A WARNING THAT WHEN GUIDANCE IS REJECTED, EASE BECOMES A PUNISHMENT, DELAY BECOMES DECEPTION, AND WORLDLY GAIN BECOMES A MEANS OF DESTRUCTION — FOR ALLAH SWT’S JUSTICE, THOUGH PATIENT, IS ALWAYS CERTAIN.
Istidraaj means gradual entrapment through apparent blessings.
It is when Allah, out of His justice and wisdom, allows a wrongdoer to prosper so that his arrogance increases and his punishment becomes fully deserved.
As the Prophet ﷺ said “When you see Allah granting a servant the worldly things he loves, despite his sins, then know that it is istidraaj (a gradual drawing to destruction).”
So, istidraaj is not mercy — it is delayed justice disguised as ease.

translation.text: I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless.
So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not be like ˹Jonah,˺ the Man of the Whale, who cried out ˹to Allah˺, in total distress.

commentary.text: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) — and all believers — are told to remain patient and steadfast, waiting for Allah’s judgment and timing.

The Prophet (PBUH) should not lose patience or act hastily when facing rejection or hardship, as Prophet Yunus once did when he left his people before Allah SWT’s permission (this was his only faut therefore Prophet Muhammad is being told repeatedly to be patient and wait for Allah SWT’s decision.) Because of that impatience, Yunus was swallowed by a great fish, finding himself in darkness and grief. Yet, when he realized his mistake, he turned to Allah SWT with humility, praying: “There is no god but You; glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.” Allah SWT accepted his repentance and rescued him.

The Ayat teaches a deep lesson: Allah SWT’s help and victory come only at the right time, through patience, perseverance, and faith. Even prophets faced tests that required trust in Allah’s wisdom. Believers, therefore, must not despair or act in haste when facing trials — instead, they should keep striving calmly, knowing that every hardship is part of Allah SWT’s perfect plan and that relief always follows patience.
FYI - Nun is also the name for a fish.

translation.text: Or do they have any knowledge of the Unseen which they are now writing down?

commentary.text: Do these deniers have knowledge of the unseen or are they scribes writing down destines.

commentary.text: Be patient O Prophet and do not be like Ayub who left his nation in anger and haste without waiting for Allah SWT’s command. If Allah SWT had not forgiven him, he would be blameworthy.

Yunus’s withdrawal led to his trial in the belly of the fish, where he turned back to Allah SWT with humility and tasbih, and only then was he rescued. By recalling this incident, Allah SWT teaches the Prophet (PBUH) that rejection and hardship are not reasons to abandon the mission or act in frustration; rather, steadfast patience, reliance on Allah SWT, and perseverance in da‘wah are the path to eventual help and victory. The lesson is that even a prophet’s moment of impatience carried consequences, so true success lies in remaining firm until Allah SWT’s judgment unfolds.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says that the disbelievers almost caused the Prophet (PBUH) to slip with their eyes when they heard the Quran. It shows that their looks were not ordinary looks but looks of envy, hatred, and malice, what the Quran describes as the evil eye. The disbelievers also called magicians who can cast spell by looks.

The scholars understood this Ayat as proof that the evil eye is real and can harm by Allah SWT’s permission, which is why many authentic hadith speak about seeking protection from it through du‘ā and ruqyah.
The curx of the matter being that the disbelievers wanted the Prophet (PBUH) to give up Islam.

They were unable to defeat the Prophet (PBUH) intellectually or morally, tried to harm him through jealousy and then accused him of madness because of the Quran. Allah SWT replies by exposing their behavior and affirming that the Quran is not madness but a reminder for all the worlds, and that their hostile looks and accusations could not harm the Prophet (PBUH) except by Allah SWT’s will. The verse therefore shows both their spiritual sickness (envy and denial) and Allah SWT’s protection of His Messenger (PBUH).

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word with which it opens.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah al-Haaqqah (The Inevitable) is an early Makki surah named after its opening word. It was revealed when opposition to the Prophet (PBUH) had begun but was not yet fully hostile. A famous incident from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) shows how its recitation moved him—he heard its warning that the Quran is not poetry or soothsaying, and the message penetrated his heart over time. It answered every question he had with an Ayat that it is not poetry or fortunetelling.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The surah has two main parts.
The overall message: The Hereafter is certain, worldly ease can deceive, and acceptance or rejection of the Quran determines lasting fate.

items.text: Ayat 1–37 Stress the reality of the Resurrection: Past nations who denied the Hereafter were destroyed. The Day of Judgment will be unmistakable, and every person’s record will be shown—those who lived with God-consciousness will rejoice, while the heedless will be doomed.

Ayat 38–52 Refute the Quran’s detractors in Makkah: The Book is divine revelation, not human invention; the Prophet (PBUH) could not add or alter it, and those who call it false will face severe regret.

sections.title: 1-18 DESCRIPTION OF THE DAY OF RESURRECTION AND THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: The Inevitable Hour!

commentary.text: The word Al-Haaqqah from Haq (truth) means an event which will most certainty occur. There is no doubt about that. To use this word for Resurrection and to begin the discourse with it by itself shows that the people were denying its occurrence. They are being told: That which you are denying is inevitable: your denial will not prevent its occurrence.

translation.text: What is the Inevitable Hour?

commentary.text: What is Al-Haqqah?
Al-Haqqah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement, because during it the promise and the threat will inevitably occur.

translation.text: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Hour is?

commentary.text: These two questions, one after the other, have been put to arouse the listeners, to make them understand the importance of the theme and listen to what follows with full attention.

translation.text: ˹Both˺ Thamûd and ’Ȃd denied the Striking Disaster.

commentary.text: Disbelievers who rejected the truth of the Resurrection is nothing new — earlier nations like Thamud and ‘Ad denied and were destroyed. Their denial was not merely disbelief but moral decay that grew from rejecting accountability before Allah SWT. When people see no life beyond this one, they lose restraint and justice, which leads to ruin.

The term “al-Qāri‘ah” literally means a striking or hammering blow. It describes the sudden, overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment — something that “strikes” hearts and worlds with terror. It emphasizes that the final calamity will come with unstoppable force, shaking creation itself, as a warning to those who take it lightly.

translation.text: As for Thamûd, they were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.

commentary.text: Violent earthquake.

translation.text: And as for ’Ȃd, they were destroyed by a furious, bitter wind
which Allah unleashed on them non-stop for seven nights and eight days, so that you would have

commentary.text: seen its people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees.

translation.text: Do you see any of them left alive?
Also, Pharaoh and those before him, and ˹the people of˺ the overturned cities ˹of Lot˺ indulged in sin,
each disobeying their Lord’s messenger, so He seized them with a crushing grip.
Indeed, when the floodwater had overflowed, We carried you in the floating Ark ˹with Noah˺,
so that We may make this a reminder to you, and that attentive ears may grasp it.

commentary.text: These Ayats remind us of the seriousness of denying faith and the Day of Judgment.
One nation after another—Thamud, ‘Ad, Pharaoh, and others—rejected their messengers and were destroyed by overwhelming calamities.

Thamud were struck by a mighty blast, ‘Ad by a violent wind lasting seven nights and eight days, leaving them fallen like hollow palm trunks. Pharaoh and those before him also disobeyed, and Allah SWT seized them with a severe grip.

The surah then shifts to the scene of resurrection, when the trumpet will sound, the earth and mountains will crumble, and the sky will split open as angels surround it. Eight mighty angels will bear the Throne of Allah SWT. These powerful images stress the gravity of accountability—some will receive their records with joy in their right hand and enter peaceful gardens, while others will face the dreadful consequences of denial.

translation.text: At last, when the Trumpet will be blown with one blast,
on that Day the Inevitable Event will have come to pass.

commentary.text: The Day of Judgment will begin.

translation.text: The sky will be torn apart on that Day, it will be so frail.
with the angels on its sides. On that Day eight ˹mighty angels˺ will bear the Throne of your Lord

commentary.text: above them.

Āyāt Mutashābihāt (آيَات مُتَشَابِهَات) are Quranic Ayats whose exact meanings are not fully known or clear to human understanding. They deal with realities of the unseen — matters like the nature of Allah SWT, the Throne (ʿArsh), the Hereafter, or the manner of divine actions — which cannot be grasped by human reason or experience.

Here we find the description of a scene beyond human understanding — the Throne and the eight angels who will bear it on the Day of Resurrection. It’s true nature is known only to Allah SWT. It does not mean that Allah Himself is seated on the Throne and being carried, for He is beyond all physical form, direction, or place. Such descriptions are symbolic, meant to convey Allah SWT’s absolute power and authority, not to be taken literally. Trying to define or imagine their true form would go beyond the limits of faith and human comprehension.

translation.text: You will then be presented ˹before Him for judgment˺, and none of your secrets will stay hidden.

commentary.text: On that Day, all will stand before Allah SWT, and nothing will remain hidden. Every secret and deed will be revealed, and people will receive their records—some in their right hand, others in their left.
Hadith: Be shy of your Raab as is befitting.

Lesson: We are too shy to sin in front of people, yet when we are alone, we sin with abandon. Always remember you are never alone and Allah SWT is always watching. Gurad, you head and your stomach from sin. Negative thoughts and filling your bellies.

sections.title: 19-37 FORTUNATE PEOPLE AND THEIR REWARD AND UNFORTUNATE PEOPLE AND THEIR PUNISHMENT

translation.text: As for those given their records in their right hand, they will cry ˹happily˺, “Here ˹everyone˺! Read my record!

commentary.text: On that Day, whoever receives their record in the right hand will know they are safe and successful.
Dua: May Allah SWT make us of those people. (Always read this dua after such an Ayat).

translation.text: I surely knew I would face my reckoning.”

commentary.text: The believer will say, “I was sure that I would meet my account.” This shows his faith and awareness in the world that he would one day stand before Allah. Because of this belief, he is saved from disgrace on the Day of Judgment.

The Prophet (PBUH) said Allah SWT will draw His servant close and remind him of all his sins until he fears destruction. Then Allah SWT will say, “I concealed these sins for you in the world, and today I forgive you.” The servant will then receive his record in his right hand.
Lesson: Live life with certainty keeping death and the Hereafter front of mind. Live life on earth like a stranger/guest.

translation.text: They will be in a life of bliss,

commentary.text: For a person who lives life keeping in mind that the Day of reckoning is close will enter paradise in sha Allah.

˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink joyfully for what you did in the days gone by.”
And as for those given their record in their left hand, they will cry ˹bitterly˺, “I wish I had not been given my record,

commentary.text: That is, I should not have been told what I had done in the world. Another meaning of this Ayat can also be: I never knew what an account was: I never had imagined that one day I would also have to render my account and that all my deeds would be presented before me.

My authority has been stripped from me.”

Lesson: DEATH IS THE LEVELER.  Purpose of life is to worship Allah SWT and not collect wealth and power. Allah SWT is the best Provider and Wali (guardian). So have tawaqul and live life as we have been commanded to.

Some scholars also view Ar-Rūḥ as the souls of mankind ascending after death.

For the disbelievers, it will be unbearably long, filled with terror and regret; but for the believers, as the Prophet (PBUH) said, it will pass like the time between two prayers.

front_matter.label: Name:
front_matter.text: The surah is named after Prophet Nūḥ (Noah), whose story forms its entire content.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation:
front_matter.text: It was revealed in Makkah during the early but intense phase of opposition to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The Makkan disbelievers’ hostility had grown, mirroring the defiance once shown by the people of Nuh.

front_matter.label: Theme and Purpose:
front_matter.text:
The surah recounts the mission of Prophet Nuh not merely as a historical account but as a warning to the Quraysh. It draws a parallel between their rejection of Muhammad (PBUH) and the rejection faced by Nuh from his people, implying that persistent disbelief will bring the same destruction.
The theme is of Dawa (preaching or calling people to Islam). It is a Surah about patience, steadfastness and hope.
There is about 10 generations or 1000 years between Adam and Nuh.
Adam was upon truth, but the later generations corrupted the truth and shirk came into existence. So Nuh was the first man to warn people. He warned them for 950 years. Allah SWT sent Nuh to warn his nation against the sin of shirkh. To stop doing shirk before it became too late and the punishment came.
Overall this time on about 80 people accepted. But Nuh did not get angry or bitter rather he was exemplary in his patience.
Content Overview:
Ayats 2–4: Nuh’s call to his people to worship Allah SWT, seek forgiveness, and turn to Him for mercy and prosperity.
Ayats 5–20: His patient preaching over centuries and the obstinate denial of his people despite repeated warnings.
While studying this Surah one should keep in view the details of the Prophet Nuh's story in Surah Al-Araf: 59-64 Yunus: 71,73, Hud: 25-49, Al-Mu'minun: 23-31, Ash- Shua'ra: 105-122, Al-Ankabut: 14,15, As-Saaffat: 75-82, Al-Qamar: 9-16.

sections.title: 1-20 PROPHET NUH'S PREACHING AND SUBMISSION TO ALLAH AFTER EXHAUSTING ALL HIS EFFORTS

translation.text: We sent Noah to his people (and directed him): “Warn your people before a grievous chastisement comes upon them.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT sent Nuh to his people commanding him to warn them of the punishment of Allah SWT before it befell them. He was to tell them that if they repent and turn to Allah SWT, then the punishment would be lifted from them.

translation.text: Noah proclaimed, “O my people! I am truly sent to you with a clear warning:

commentary.text: Meaning the clarity of the warning, was apparent and clear.

translation.text: worship Allah ˹alone˺, fear Him, and obey me.

commentary.text: The three things Prophet Nuh preached:

(1) Worship of Allah SWT alone! Worship of Allah meant that they should give up worship and service of all others and should acknowledge Allah alone as their Deity and should worship and carry out His commands alone.

(2) Adoption of piety (taqwa). Taqwa (piety) meant that they should refrain from all those things which cause Allah SWT’s anger and displeasure and should instead adopt such attitude in their lives as the God-fearing people should adopt. To Sin and Refuse to obey, i.e. Doing what is prohibited shows arrogance and lack of conviction.
(3) Obedience of the Messenger. As for “obey me”, it meant that they should obey the commands that he gave them as Allah SWT’s Messenger/Representative.
FYI: Nabi does not say obey me. He says adopt faith/Iman etc etc. For example, Prophet Yousuf was a Nabi.
DAWA: Should not be complicated rather stress on key salient points.

translation.text: He will forgive your sins and delay your end until the appointed time. Indeed, when the time set by Allah comes, it cannot be delayed, if only you knew!”

commentary.text: This Ayat conveys both mercy and warning in Prophet Nūḥ’s call.
The promise of forgiveness of past sins if the people accept faith, repent, and obey Allah SWT.

However, when Allah SWT’s decreed time for punishment arrives, it cannot be delayed or averted. Once divine judgment is set in motion, even belief at that moment cannot save a people. The closing phrase — “if you only knew” — stresses that this period of safety and prosperity is a temporary reprieve, urging immediate repentance before the final decree takes effect.

FYI: Here not all sins is mentioned meaning that those sins we commit against other people (for example slander or back biting) we will be held accountable for on the DoJ and there will be the transaction of debt and credit there.

translation.text: He cried, “My Lord! I have surely called my people day and night,
but my calls only made them run farther away.
And whenever I invite them to be forgiven by You, they press their fingers into their ears, cover themselves with their clothes, persist ˹in denial˺, and act very arrogantly.

commentary.text: Here the extreme stubbornness of Nuh’s people is vividly captured. His invitation was not merely to belief but to forgiveness — moral renewal through repentance — yet they responded with deliberate avoidance.

They plugged their ears to block the message and covered their faces either out of contempt or to avoid being recognized and called again. This physical rejection symbolizes a deeper spiritual resistance. Their pride (istikbār) made them see submission to divine truth as beneath their dignity, just as the Quraysh later treated the Prophet
Thus, arrogance blinds the heart: refusing to even hear the truth, let alone reflect upon it, becomes the first step toward moral ruin and divine rejection.
Obstinate and persistent denial and arrogance.

translation.text: Then I certainly called them openly,
and preached to them in public and also addressed them in secret.

commentary.text: DAWA: Tactics or strategies of doing Dawa: Open and or secret. Change tactics as needed. Become innovative.

translation.text: I said to them: “Ask forgiveness from your Lord; surely He is Most Forgiving.
He will shower you with abundant rain,

commentary.text: Here we find the link or connection between Allah SWT’s mercy and istighfār (seeking forgiveness) and divine blessings.

Prophet Nūḥ’s call to his people shows that repentance not only erases sins but also brings tangible worldly benefits — here symbolized by midrār (continuous, abundant rain), which implies prosperity, renewal, and sustenance.

Early Muslims, including ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, understood this connection; during a drought, he led the prayer for rain by reciting these Ayats and focusing solely on istighfār, saying, “I have sought rain with the keys of the heavens.”
Lesson:  Sincere repentance = Forgiveness + Blessings in Both Worlds. IA
Istakfar opens doors of Allah SWT Mercy and Forgiveness and Provision in this world and the Next. IA
Dua: Allah Huma Maghfirli, (FORGIVENESS) Hammni (MERCY), Afini (SAFETY), Zuqni (PROVIOSION).
When we are stuck or have issues do istakfar. Many scholars including Basri told their students to do istakfar. Why they asked and he recited these Ayats 10, 11 and 12.

translation.text: and will provide you with wealth and children, and will bestow upon you gardens and rivers.

commentary.text: Prophet Nūḥ assures his people that repentance (istighfār) is not only a path to forgiveness but also to renewal and prosperity in this world. If they turn sincerely to Allah SWT, He will open the skies with abundant rain, bless their lands, crops, and livestock, and grant them familial joy and sustenance.

The Quran elsewhere reinforces this link between faith and flourishing — that piety and obedience bring blessings, while disbelief and corruption lead to deprivation. Also see Surah Hūd (11:3, 52) and Al-Aʿrāf (7:96).
Lesson: Rejecting Allah SWT’s mercy blocks the very sources of prosperity and turns life’s potential abundance into barrenness.
DAWA: Should entail warnings but also incentives of Mercy, Forgiveness and Worldly Benefits.

translation.text: What is the matter with you that you are not in awe of the Majesty of Allah,

commentary.text: Why do you not put your belief and hope in Allah SWT? What is the matter with you?
You rebel against Him, associate others in His Divinity, disobey His commands, and yet you are not at all afraid that He would punish you for your misconduct??
Lesson: Put your trust in the Creator and not Creation.

translation.text: when He truly created you in stages ˹of development˺?

commentary.text: Reflect on the miraculous process of human creation and development. It reminds humanity that life unfolds through deliberate, divinely guided stages — from the joining of sperm and ovum to formation in the womb, birth, growth, maturity, and finally old age.

Each stage displays human dependence on Allah SWT’s will and power. At any point, He could have altered or ended one’s life — preventing conception, impairing the body, or halting growth. This reflection exposes the absurdity of arrogance: how can a being so utterly dependent on divine mercy rebel against the One who formed him with such precision?
Lesson: Be grateful and humble. Understand your position.

translation.text: Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens, one above the other,
placing the moon within them as a ˹reflected˺ light, and the sun as a ˹radiant˺ lamp?
Allah ˹alone˺ caused you to grow from the earth like a plant.

commentary.text: Here, the creation of man out of the substances of the earth has been compared to the growth of vegetation. Just as at one time there was no vegetation on the earth, then Allah SWT caused it to grow, so at one time man did not exist, then Allah SWT created him.
Lesson: This might be an indication for the Darwin theory, but we don’t know.

translation.text: Then He will return you to it, and then simply bring you forth ˹again˺.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgement, He will repeat your creation just as He first originated you.

translation.text: And Allah ˹alone˺ spread out the earth for you
to walk along its spacious pathways.

commentary.text: Allah SWT made the earth spacious and easy to travel, showing His mercy and power. Its paths, lands, and resources are blessings meant to help humanity live and prosper, calling people to worship and thank the One Creator who made it all.
DAWA: Nuh showing people Allah SWT’s favors so that they turn to Him. (i) our bodies (ii) Sky (iii) Moon and Sun (iv) Earth that is vast.

translation.text: ˹Eventually,˺ Noah cried, “My Lord! They have certainly persisted in disobeying me, and followed ˹instead˺ those ˹elite˺ whose ˹abundant˺ wealth and children only increase them in loss,

commentary.text: Prophet Nūḥ’s sorrowful plea to Allah SWT after centuries of preaching. Despite his tireless efforts—calling his people with kindness, warning, and sincerity—they rejected his message and chose to follow the arrogant wealthy whose riches and children only deepened their loss.
It exposes the folly of those who measure success by worldly gain rather than faith, reminding that wealth and status, when divorced from righteousness, become means of ruin rather than honor.

translation.text: and who have devised a tremendous plot,

commentary.text: Here the elaborate schemes devised by the leaders of Nūḥ’s people to discredit him and dissuade others from accepting his message. Their “tremendous plot” involved mockery, misinformation, and social manipulation—calling Nūḥ a mere man, dismissing his followers as lowly, and claiming that if his message were true, angels or miracles would have been sent instead.
These tactics mirror those used later by the Quraysh against Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
LESSON: EVEN TODAY THE ELITE ARE FOLLOWED AND MIMICKED BY THE MASSES. REFLECT ON WHO YOU OBSESS OVER AND FOLLOW.

translation.text: urging ˹their followers˺, ‘Do not abandon your idols—especially Wadd, Suwâ’, Yaghûth, Ya’ûq, and Nasr.’

commentary.text: Nūḥ’s people schemed to preserve idol worship and resist his message. Their leaders urged loyalty to ancient idols—Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, and Nasr—which were first named after righteous men. After those men died, statues were made in their memory, and with time they became objects of worship.
Ibn ʿAbbās explained that these same idols later appeared among the Arabs, proving how misplaced reverence and tradition can lead generations into shirk (idolatry).
Lesson: Beware of going to graves or shrines to seek guidance or worship. This is SHIRK.

translation.text: Those ˹elite˺ have already led many astray. So ˹O Lord˺, only allow the wrongdoers to stray farther away.”

commentary.text: Prophet Nūḥ’s final appeal to Allah SWT after centuries of rejection. His people’s idol worship had not only destroyed their own faith but also misled generations that followed.
As Ibn Kathīr explains, these idols became sources of misguidance among later nations — Arabs, non-Arabs, and the descendants of Adam — showing how one act of shirk can spread through history.

Realizing that further respite would only deepen their corruption, Nūḥ prayed that Allah SWT grant the wrongdoers no increase except in error meaning do not now let them accept faith and have Your Mercy similar to when Prophet Musa requested Allah SWT that Pharon should not accept faith rather only increase him in destruction so that he burns in Hell. This was a righteous plea aligned with divine justice, much like the supplications of Prophet Ibrāhīm — “They have indeed led astray many among mankind” (14:36) — and Prophet Mūsā — “Destroy their wealth and harden their hearts” (10:88).
Allah SWT answered Nūḥ’s prayer as He had those of earlier prophets: the wrongdoers, persisting in disbelief and arrogance, were drowned and cut off from all means of guidance.

translation.text: So because of their sins, they were drowned, then admitted into the Fire. And they found none to help them against Allah.

commentary.text: Drowning was not their end, but after death their souls were immediately subjected to the punishment of the Fire. So they were carried from the flood of the seas to the heat of the fire of Hell. This precisely was the treatment that was meted out to Pharaoh and his people, as has been stated in Surah Al-Momin, Ayats 45-46.
This Ayat also is of those Ayats which prove the punishment of barzakh (intermediary stage between death and Resurrection).

translation.text: Noah had prayed, “My Lord! Do not leave a single disbeliever on earth.

commentary.text: Do not leave a single one of them on the face of the earth, not even a lone individual.
FYI – Nuh’s own son was also killed as he had turned his back to Iman.

commentary.text: If You leave a single one of them they will lead your servants astray.
Lesson: Who are you surrounding yourself with?

translation.text: My Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house in faith, and ˹all˺ believing men and women. And increase the wrongdoers only in destruction.”

commentary.text: Prophet Nūḥ’s supplication begins with personal humility, seeking forgiveness for himself and his parents, then expands to all who shared his faith — “whoever enters my house in faith”. Then widens further to embrace the entire believing community, living and dead, illustrating the Prophet’s universal compassion and the continuity of belief across generations.
The final plea — “increase he wrongdoers only in destruction ” — contrasts sharply with his earlier prayers for mercy. After exhaustive efforts to guide his people for 950 years.
Utter loss in both worlds, reflects not vengeance but recognition that persistence in disbelief nullifies the possibility of reform.
