titles: 1-15 A BEAUTIFUL SPEECH OF THE JINNS WHO EMBRACED ISLAM AFTER HEARING AL-QURAN AND JINNS ALSO HAVE DIFFERENT RELIGIONS AND SECTS, AMONG JINNS THERE ARE SOME MUSLIMS AND SOME DEVIATORS FROM THE TRUTH
16-19 MOSQUES ARE BUILT FOR THE WORSHIP OF ALLAH, SO INVOKE NO ONE ELSE BESIDES HIM
20-28 RASOOLS DO NOT HAVE THE POWER TO HARM OR BENEFIT ANYONE, HIS MISSION IS JUST TO CONVEY ALLAH'S MESSAGE AND ONLY ALLAH KNOWS THE UNSEEN, HE REVEALS IT TO WHOM HE CHOOSES FROM

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The surah takes its name from the word “Al-Jinn”, mentioned at the beginning, and its central theme — the encounter of a group of jinn who listened to the Quran and returned to their people to convey its message.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Jinn was revealed early in the Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) mission, in Makkah. The incident occurred when he was traveling to the Fair of ʿUkāẓ and stopped at a place called Nakhlah to offer the Fajr (dawn) prayer. A group of jinn happened to pass by and heard him reciting the Quran. They were so deeply affected by what they heard that they believed in the message and went back to tell other jinn about it.
Some later scholars thought this event happened during the Prophet’s journey to Ṭāʾif (which took place much later, around the 10th year of Prophethood). However, evidence shows that these were two different events:
The jinn in Surah Al-Aḥqāf (46:29–32) were already believers in earlier revelations like the Torah, while the jinn in Surah Al-Jinn were idol worshippers who accepted Islam after hearing the Quran.
During the Ṭāʾif journey, the Prophet (PBUH) traveled only with Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, but Ibn ʿAbbās reports that during the event of Surah Al-Jinn, the Prophet had other companions with him.
So, this event in Surah Al-Jinn took place earlier in Makkah—shortly after the Prophet’s (PBUH) mission began—when the jinn first sensed great cosmic changes caused by his prophethood and came to investigate.

front_matter.label: Context and Significance
front_matter.text:
Before the Prophet’s (PBUH) advent, the jinn were able to eavesdrop on heavenly discussions, but once revelation began, they found the skies guarded by angels and flaming meteors. Realizing something momentous had occurred on earth, they searched until one group heard the Prophet’s recitation of the Quran — recognizing it as the divine message that had caused the heavens to be sealed.
Thus, Surah Al-Jinn presents one of the earliest confirmations of the Prophet’s (PBUH) mission, showing that the impact of the Quran transcends human audiences, drawing belief even from the unseen world.

front_matter.label: Reality of the Jinn
front_matter.text:
The jinn are real beings created by Allah SWT, different from humans and hidden from our sight. Some modern people deny their existence, thinking only what can be seen or measured is real. But this belief is narrow, because the Quran teaches that unseen realities also exist, such as Allah SWT, paradise/hell, angels, and the jinn.
The Quran clearly distinguishes humans and jinn as two separate creations. Humans were made from clay, while the jinn were made from smokeless fire. The jinn existed before humans, and they can see us while we cannot see them. Although they can move quickly and reach parts of the heavens, they cannot go beyond what Allah allows or gain knowledge of the unseen.
Like humans, the jinn have free will. Some believe in Allah SWT and follow His guidance, while others reject the truth and follow Satan. They too will be judged for their deeds. The Quran also tells us that the jinn once tried to mislead humans and were even worshipped by some Arabs before Islam.
In many Surahs of the Quran Allah SWT addresses mankind and the Jinn, for example, in Surah Rahman.
In short, the jinn are part of Allah SWT’s unseen creation—real beings with power and choice—but not divine or beyond His control. Jinn can see and hear us but we cannot see or hear them. They can cause us physical harm, but we can protect ourselves via duas and zikr. Jinn feed on bones so throw bones in the dustbin.

front_matter.label: Summary and Analysis:
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Jinn recounts how a group of jinn heard the Quran, recognized its truth, and embraced faith, declaring Allah SWTs oneness and rejecting falsehood (1–15). Their response affirms the Quran’s divine origin and universal message.
The later Ayats (16–28) warn humans—especially the disbelievers of Makkah—that righteousness brings blessings while disbelief leads to punishment. The Prophet (PBUH) is reminded that his duty is only to convey the message, as all knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah SWT alone. The surah contrasts the jinn’s quick acceptance of truth with human arrogance, emphasizing divine authority, humility, and accountability.

sections.title: 1-15 A BEAUTIFUL SPEECH OF THE JINNS WHO EMBRACED ISLAM AFTER HEARING AL-QURAN AND JINNS ALSO HAVE DIFFERENT RELIGIONS AND SECTS, AMONG JINNS THERE ARE SOME MUSLIMS AND SOME DEVIATORS FROM THE TRUTH

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened ˹to the Quran,˺ and said ˹to their fellow jinn˺: ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous recitation.

commentary.text: This shows that the jinn at that time were not visible to the Prophet (PBUH), nor did he know that they were hearing the Quran being recited, but Allah SWT informed him of the incident afterwards by revelation.

translation.text: It leads to Right Guidance so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord ˹in worship˺.

commentary.text: This is the response of the jinn when they first heard the Quran. Their quick acceptance of tawḥīd (oneness of God) after hearing the Quran highlights the universal reach of the Quran’s message. The Quran should transform a person. For the Jinn one encounter with the Quran transformed them.
Key points about the jinn:
They already believed in Allah SWT as Creator and Sustainer but, like humans, some had fallen into polytheism.
The jinn do not receive their own prophets or scriptures; instead, they are guided through the revelations sent to human messengers.

arabic_lines: وَّ اَنَّهٗ كَانَ يَقُوۡلُ سَفِيۡهُنَا عَلَى اللّٰهِ شَطَطًا ۙ

translation.text: Now, we believe that˺ our Lord—Exalted is His Majesty—has neither taken a mate nor offspring,

commentary.text: From this we know two things:
(1) That these jinn were either from among the Christian jinn, or they were followers of a different religion in which Allah SWT was regarded as having children and families.

(2) At that time the Prophet (PBUH) was reciting some such part of the Quran. Upon hearing the Quran, they realized the error of their creed and knew that it was sheer ignorance and disrespect to ascribe a wife and children to the High and Exalted Being of Allah SWT.
FYI – Now every Ayat begins with وَّ اَنَّهٗ because Allah SWT is quoting what the jinn themselves said after hearing the Quran. The conversation between the Jinn’s continues from here till Ayat 16.

translation.text: and that the foolish of us used to utter ˹outrageous˺ falsehoods about Allah.

commentary.text: The believing jinn admit that before hearing the Quran, the “foolish among us” meaning Iblis and his followers would utter grave falsehoods about Allah SWT, such as claiming He had a partner or a son. They now recognize these as terrible lies and turn to pure monotheism, showing how the Quran corrected their false beliefs and guided them to truth.

translation.text: We certainly thought that humans and jinn would never speak lies about Allah.

commentary.text: That is, we (Jinn) were misled by those falsehoods because we could never think that the men or the jinn could ever dare forge a lie about Allah SWT but having heard this Quran, we now know that they were, in fact, liars.
So, when we heard this Quran, we knew that they (Jinns and men) had been lying about Allah SWT in this matter.
Lesson: Gain Knowledge yourself so that no one can utter a lie against our Creator and we believe it.

translation.text: And some men used to seek refuge with some jinn—so they increased each other in wickedness.

commentary.text: Before Islam, Arabs commonly sought protection from jinn when camping or traveling through desolate places.

When humans began fearing and invoking jinn for safety, the jinn became arrogant and bold. Instead of offering protection, they deepened human fear and led them further astray. This sin or transgression of seeking refuge from others besides Allah SWT increased both groups in wrongdoing.

This Ayat exposes how misplaced dependence on the jinn corrupts belief, making people subservient to false powers. It reminds humanity that true protection and refuge belong only to Allah SWT, not to any unseen beings or intermediaries.

Lesson: Never be sacred of Jinn and give them the power of feeling superior.  We as humans are superior to every creator so act like it. Read dua below and Ayat Al Kursi and other zikr. Close doors with BismillAllah as that shuts out satan.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
Ā‘ūdhu bi kalimātillāhi at-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
Meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect Words of Allah SWT from the evil of what He has created.

translation.text: And those ˹humans˺ thought, just like you ˹jinn˺, that Allah would not resurrect anyone ˹for judgment˺.

commentary.text: This Ayat shows that before hearing the Quran, both humans and jinn had believed that Allah SWT would not send any new messenger. Some even denied resurrection, thinking divine revelation had ended. During this time disbelief spread.

When the jinn heard the Quran, they realized this assumption was false—the heavens had been guarded because Allah SWT had indeed appointed a new Prophet. Thus, their statement affirmed that revelation and divine guidance were continuing through Muhammad (PBUH).

translation.text: ˹Earlier˺ we tried to reach heaven ˹for news˺, only to find it filled with stern guards and shooting stars.
We used to take up positions there for eavesdropping, but whoever dares eavesdrop now will find a flare lying in wait for them.

commentary.text: Allah SWT informs about the Jinns when He sent His Messenger Muhammad and revealed the Quran to him. Among the ways He protected it (the Quran) was by filling sky with stern guards guarding it from all its sides and strict security measures against eavesdropping.

The devils were then expelled from the places where they used to sit prior to that. This was so that they could not steal anything from the Quran and tell it to the soothsayers, thereby causing matters to be confused and mixed up.

translation.text: Now, we do not really know whether evil is intended for those on earth, or their Lord intends for them what is right.

commentary.text: When the jinn, witnessed the heavens suddenly guarded and meteors blazing across the sky, wondered whether Allah SWT intended punishment for those on earth or guidance through a new revelation.

This extraordinary heavenly activity began when Allah SWT decreed the revelation of the Quran and protected it from the devils who once eavesdropped on the angels. Alarmed by this new barrier, the jinn searched across the earth for its cause and eventually found the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) reciting the Quran at Nakhlah. They realized that this revelation—not destruction—was the reason for the celestial change.
Some of them believed, understanding that Allah SWT intended guidance while others remained defiant.

translation.text: Among us are those who are righteous and those who are less so. We have been of different paths

commentary.text: The Jinns testify that among Them there are Believers, Disbelievers, Misguided and Guided
After hearing the Qur’an, the jinn acknowledged the diversity within their ranks.
This reveals that, like humans, the jinn consist of believers and disbelievers, the guided and the misguided, each following different ideologies and inclinations, moral and spiritual division.

A narration from al-Aʿmash further illustrates this human-like diversity: when a jinn was asked whether sectarian differences existed among them, he confirmed that they did, adding that the Rāfiḍah were considered the worst among them.

Recognizing the truth, the jinn then confessed Allah SWT’s complete authority, declaring: “We knew that we could never escape Allah SWT on earth, nor could we elude Him by flight.” This reflects their understanding that no creature—visible or unseen—can defy or evade divine control.
Together, these Ayats affirm that the jinn, like humankind, possess free will, moral accountability, and exist under Allah’s absolute dominion.

translation.text: ˹Now,˺ we truly know that we cannot frustrate Allah on earth, nor can we escape from Him ˹into heaven˺.

commentary.text: The jinn realized that Allah SWT’s power is absolute and inescapable; none can flee His control. Aware of this, they abandoned false beliefs and submitted to the truth revealed by Allah SWT.

translation.text: When we heard the guidance ˹of the Quran˺, we ˹readily˺ believed in it. For whoever believes in their Lord will have no fear of being denied ˹a reward˺ or wronged.

commentary.text: When the jinn heard the message of truth, they believed in it, realizing that faith in Allah SWT ensures complete justice. A believer need not fear loss or injustice—Allah SWT neither withholds due reward nor punishes beyond what is deserved.

translation.text: And among us are those who have submitted ˹to Allah˺ and those who are deviant. So ˹as for˺ those who submitted, it is they who have attained Right Guidance.
And as for the deviant, they will be fuel for Hell.’

sections.title: 16-19 MOSQUES ARE BUILT FOR THE WORSHIP OF ALLAH, SO INVOKE NO ONE ELSE BESIDES HIM

translation.text: Had the deniers followed the Right Way, We would have certainly granted them abundant rain to drink—

commentary.text: Also see Surah Nuh Ayat 10
The conversation of the jinn having come to an end, with this begins the speech of Allah SWT.
This is an early Meccan Surah. The Jinn are being presented as an example for mankind. If the Quraish (we/mankind) believe we will be given provision in this world as well.

Abundance of water has been used for abundance of blessings metaphorically for human life, and habitations also depend on water. Without water there can be no human settlement, nor can man’s basic needs be fulfilled, nor his industries work and prosper.
Lesson: For those who believe there is no fear and Allah SWT blesses us in this world and the next.

translation.text: as a test for them. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of their Lord will be admitted by Him into an overwhelming punishment.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says He might try them by that blessing to see whether they remain grateful after having received the blessing or not, and whether they put these blessing to right use or not.
Those who turn away from or reject the advice and admonition sent down by Allah SWT will face a huge punishment.

Lesson: Obedience in this world does not mean suffering because Allah SWT will give. But the blessings then become a test as to how grateful we are and if we use the blessings in the right way. While for non-believers blessing are a test to make them fall more into sin. Either way blessings are TEST.
Remember ease in not with things.
Hadith: Allah SWT says make time for worship and your needs will be fulfilled and your heart will be filled.
Allah SWT creates ease. Thus, rejecting Allah SWT will not make life easy.
Often what we think is a blessing is not what Allah SWT defines as a blessing.
Lesson: The choice to turn away or embrace guidance is ours and the consequences profound.

translation.text: The places of worship are ˹only˺ for Allah, so do not invoke anyone besides Him.

commentary.text: The commentators generally have taken mosques to mean the places of worship and our limbs used to prostrate. None should be associated in the worship of Allah SWT in the places of worship.

translation.text: Only when they see what they have been threatened with will they know who is weaker in helpers and inferior in manpower.

commentary.text: The background of this Ayat is that those of the Quraish who used to mob and surround the Prophet (PBUH) as soon as they heard his invitation calling to Allah SWT that they were under the delusion that they had a strong band and that the Prophet (PBUH) had only a handful of men with him, and therefore, they would easily overwhelm him.

At this it is being said: Today these people find the Messenger (PBUH) helpless and friendless and they themselves supported and strengthened by great hosts and, therefore, feel encouraged and emboldened to suppress the invitation to the truth. But when the evil time with which they are being threatened comes, they will know who in fact is helpless and friendless.

translation.text: Say, “I do not know if what you are promised is near or my Lord has set a distant time for it.

commentary.text: The style itself shows that this is an answer which has been given without citing the question. Probably, hearing what has been said above, the opponents might have asked mockingly and tauntingly: When will the time come with which you are threatening us.

In response, the Prophet (PBUH) was commanded to say: The time will certainly come, but I have not been told the date of its coming. Allah SWT alone knows whether it will come soon or whether a distant term has been set for it.

translation.text: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the unseen, disclosing none of it to anyone,

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is named after the word “Al-Muzzammil” in its opening Ayat, meaning “the one wrapped up.” It serves as a name, not a description of its theme.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The Surah was revealed in two parts at different times.
Ayats 1–19: Revealed in Makkah, during the early phase of Prophethood, when the Prophet (PBUH) was being spiritually prepared for his mission.
These Ayats instruct him to stand in night prayer (Tahajjud), recite the Quran, and remain patient with those who opposed him.
Ayat 20: Believed by most scholars to be Madinan, as it mentions Zakah (charity) and fighting in Allah SWTs cause, which were established later in Madinah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
In the opening Ayats (1–7), the Prophet (PBUH) is commanded to prepare for his divine mission through night prayer (Tahajjud)—standing in worship for about half the night to strengthen his spirit for the heavy responsibility of revelation.
Ayats (8–14) urge him to devote himself fully to Allah SWT, trust Him completely, and remain patient before the hostility of his opponents. He is told to avoid close ties with them and leave their fate to Allah, who will deal with them Himself.
Ayats (15–19) warn the disbelievers of Makkah, reminding them of Pharaoh’s destruction when he rejected the Messenger of Allah, and cautioning them about the punishment of the Hereafter if they persist in disbelief.
The second section (Ayat 20) was revealed about ten years later, relaxing the earlier command of long night prayers. Muslims were told to pray as much as they can at night, but to focus on the five daily prayers, give Zakah, and spend in charity sincerely for Allah’s sake.
The Surah ends by reminding believers that every good deed they perform is a lasting investment for the Hereafter, far better than what they leave behind in this world, for Allah will reward them abundantly.
It is the pair of Surah 74. And from here onwards All Surahs will be in pairs.

sections.title: 1-19 ALLAH ORDERED THE PROPHET NOT TO STAND IN PRAYER THE WHOLE NIGHT AND THOSE WHO OPPOSE THE PROPHET WILL BE TREATED WITH HEAVY FETTERS AND BLAZING FIRE AND AL-QURAN IS A REMINDER FOR THOSE WHO WANT TO FIND THE RIGHT WAY

translation.text: O you the (sleeping) enwrapped one!

commentary.text: To address the Prophet (PBUH) with these words and then to command him to rise and keep standing in the Prayer at night, shows that at the time he either lay asleep, or had wrapped himself up in a sheet to go to sleep. This is a very affectionate way to address the Prophet (PBUH). We wrap ourselves up for comfort and security.

Here, the address gives the meaning: ‘Gone is the time when you used to enjoy peaceful sleep at will; now you lie under the burden of a great mission, whose demands and duties are different as well as onerous.’
Also see (17:79)
And in some parts of the night offer the Salah with it (the Qur'an), as an additional prayer for you. It may be that your Lord will raise you to Maqam Mahmud.

translation.text: Stand up in Prayer by night, all but a small part of it;

commentary.text: Allah SWT is commanding His Prophet (PBUH) to stand up to pray. Get out of the warm, snuggly blanket. This is a Mecci Surah so one of the first things the Prophet (PBUH) was told.
Here Allah SWT explains how much prayer the Prophet (PBUH) should perform.
This can have two meanings:
(1) Pass the night standing up in the Prayer and spend only a little of it in sleep.
(2) There is no demand from you to pass the whole night in the Prayer but have rest as well and spend a little part of the night in worship too.

But in view of the theme that follows the first meaning seems to be more relevant, and the same is supported by Surah Ad-Dahr, Ayat 26, in which it has been said: Prostrate yourself before Him in the night and glorify Him during the long hours of night.

translation.text: ˹pray˺ half the night, or a little less,

commentary.text: Half the night means, instead of the whole night.

arabic_lines: اَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ الۡقُرۡاٰنَ تَرۡتِيۡلً

translation.text: or a little more—and recite the Quran ˹properly˺ in a measured way.

commentary.text: The Ayat establishes both the recommended duration and the proper manner of night devotion.
The Prophet (PBUH) is granted flexibility—half the night, or slightly more or less—yet the linguistic structure indicates that half the night remains the preferred measure.

The command to “recite the Quran slowly and distinctly” (tartīl) signifies a methodical, contemplative recitation that integrates phonetic clarity with spiritual reflection. Classical reports describe the Prophet’s practice: elongating sounds, pausing at the end of each Ayat, articulating every word with precision, and responding to the thematic cues within the Ayats—glorification where appropriate, supplication where indicated, and seeking refuge where required.
The cumulative implication is that Quranic recitation is not a mechanical act, but an intentional, reflective engagement aimed at internalizing divine guidance.
TAHAJJUD PRAYER: PRAY 8 RAKAT AND THEN RECITE THE QURAN. THIS IS BETTER THAN DOING ZIKR OR ANY OTHER FORM OF WORSHIP.

translation.text: ˹For˺ We will soon send upon you a weighty revelation.

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells the Prophet (PBUH) to stand in night prayer because a very heavy and serious message—the Quran—is about to be revealed to him. To carry this responsibility, he must strengthen his inner self through long night worship, even if it means sacrificing rest.
The Quran is called a “weighty revelation” because living by it, spreading it to the world, and transforming society through it is the greatest task ever given to a human being.

It is also “weighty” in a literal sense: the Prophet (PBUH) physically felt the heaviness of revelation. His companions described how his body would become extremely heavy, how sweat would appear on his forehead even in cold weather, and how his camel would sink to the ground under the weight of the revelation.

FYI – Night prayer and worship (idahdah) crush human desires and wants just like fasting. And the intense absorption of the Quran during the night is unparallel as there is calm, peace and a direct link.
So connect with the Quran at night with tarteel, tajweed, tafseer and tabadur.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الَّيۡلِ هِىَ اَشَدُّ وَطۡـاً وَّاَقۡوَمُ قِيۡلً

translation.text: Indeed, worship in the night is more impactful and suitable for recitation.

commentary.text: The rising for worship at night, especially after some sleep, is spiritually more powerful and effective than daytime worship. The phrase nashi’at al-layl نَاشِئَةَ الَّيۡلِ  includes the hours of the night and the act of rising during them, highlighting voluntary night prayer when comfort of the bed is hardest to leave. A time characterized by heightened internal concentration and linguistic precision.

Such worship is ashaddu waṭ’an اَشَدُّ وَطۡـاً  because it disciplines the self, restrains desires, and trains the believer in sincerity and steadfastness, free from display or hypocrisy. In the stillness of night, the heart and tongue become aligned, making recitation more truthful and impactful. For this reason, Allah SWT describes night worship as aqwamu qīlā وَّاَقۡوَمُ قِيۡلً meaning that Qur’anic recitation at this time is clearer, more upright, and deeper in understanding, as the mind is calm and distractions are absent.

Nocturnal devotion most effectively stabilizes the heart, disciplines the tongue, and facilitates accurate, contemplative recitation. This renders night worship the optimal environment for absorbing and internalizing the Quranic message.

Lesson: Night prayer is how to build strength as it is a spiritual workout. When was the last time you stood up in night prayer? Make it a habit to do it often. At night become a stranger to people and devote urself to Allah SWT.

translation.text: For during the day you are over-occupied ˹with worldly duties˺.

commentary.text: The reason for night prayer and reflection/recitation of the Quran is because during the day one is occupied/distracted with worldly endeavors, i.e., work, house, children etc.
Lesson: Night or after Fajr devotion.

arabic_lines: وَاذۡكُرِ اسۡمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلۡ اِلَيۡهِ تَبۡتِيۡلًا ؕ

translation.text: So remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with exclusive devotion.

commentary.text: After making mention of the occupation of the daytime, the call to remember the name of your Lord by itself gives the meaning: Never be heedless of the remembrance of your Lord even when you are deeply involved in your worldly occupations and continue to always commemorate His name in one way or another. (For explanation, see (Surah Al-Ahzab Ayat 33).
Tabattul: Complete devotion to Allah SWT.
Lesson: Throughout the day keep your tongue moist with zikr of Allah SWT.
BE WITH EVERYONE AND YET BE WITH NO ONE!! Always retain your own individuality in your Iman because on the DoJ you will be ALONE.

arabic_lines: رَبُّ الۡمَشۡرِقِ وَالۡمَغۡرِبِ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذۡهُ وَكِيۡلًا

translation.text: He is the Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but He. So take Him alone for your Guardian

commentary.text: The command is to worship and obey and rely upon Allah SWT exclusively.
Wakil or guardian is a person in whom one has complete faith; so much so that one can without any hesitation entrust all his affairs to him.

Thus, the Ayat means: Do not feel distressed at the hardships that you are experiencing at the storm of opposition that has been provoked by your invitation to the faith. Your Lord is He Who is the Owner of the East and the West, (i.e. of the whole universe) besides Whom no one else possesses the powers of Godhead. Entrust your affair to Him and be satisfied that He will fight your case, He will deal with your opponents, and He will look after all your interests well.
THESE ABOVE NINE AYAT ARE SUPPOSED TO BE THE THIRD REVELATION THAT CAME TO THE PROPHET (PBUH)

translation.text: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say and depart from them courteously.

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) is told to be patient because people would mock him. It will hurt so Allah SWT advices patience and courteously no matter what.

“Depart from them,” does not mean break off all ties with them and stop preaching to them, but it means: Do not have intimate and or have friendly relations with them, disregard their foolish behavior and their nonsense.
However, you should do so without showing any grief, anger or temper but gracefully like a noble person, who would disregard the abusive remarks of a mean person without minding them at all.

This should not create the misunderstanding that the Prophet’s (PBUH) conduct was any different from it, therefore, Allah SWT gave him this instruction. As a matter of fact, the Prophet (PBUH) was already following this very mode of conduct.

This instruction was given in the Quran so as to tell the disbelievers: It is not due to any weakness on the part of the Prophet (PBUH) that he is not responding to what you are saying against him, but Allah SWT Himself has taught His Messenger (PBUH) to adopt this noble way of conduct in response to your foolish behavior. And also, to leave the door open for any chance of their changing their mind and accepting.
Lesson: Lesson for life as well. Ignore and leave/avoid but with grace. If someone is talking about you or hurting, you don’t get into a fight. Ask Allah SWT for help.

translation.text: Leave it to Me to deal with the affluent ones who give the lie (to the Truth), and bear with them for a while.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says let me deal with the deniers. This is a very severe and serious threat/warning.

The well-to-do, prosperous and affluent people, found Islams message conflicting with their interests, and power structure. They forgot/denied the One who is providing them with all the comforts of life.
The Quran tells us that this was not peculiar only to the Prophet’s case but in every age this very class of the people have been the main obstacle to every movement of reform.
For example, Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 60, Surah Al-Mominoon, Ayat 33, Surah Saba, Ayats 34, 35; Surah Az-Zukhruf, Ayat 23.
Lesson: Even today the so-called liberal elite are the front runners against Islam. Under the guise of modernity and westernism they reject and mock.

translation.text: We have heavy fetters and a blazing Fire in store for them;
and a food that chokes, and a grievous chastisement.

commentary.text: This means food that will get stuck in the throat and it will not enter or come out.

translation.text: on the Day the earth and mountains will shake ˹violently˺, and mountains will be ˹reduced to˺ dunes of shifting sand.
Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.

commentary.text: The address now turns to the disbelievers of Makkah, who were denying the Prophet (PBUH) and persecuting him relentlessly. Allah SWT is asking them why they are doing that because the Prophet (PBUH) will testify to what they did on the DoJ.

Sending the Prophet (PBUH) to be a witness over the people also means that he should testify to the truth by his word and deed before them in the world and that in the Hereafter when Allah SWT’s court is established -- he will testify that he had presented the whole truth in the world.

translation.text: But Pharaoh disobeyed Our Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible seizing.

commentary.text: The example of Pharon is being given to the people of Mecca, that is, take lesson and don’t be like that or else you too will suffer the same fate.

translation.text: If you ˹pagans˺ persist in disbelief, then how will you guard yourselves against ˹the horrors of˺ a Day which will turn children’s hair grey?

commentary.text: That is, in the first place, you should be afraid that if you do not accept the invitation of the Messenger (PBUH) sent by Us, you will have to meet the same evil end in this world, which the Pharaoh has already met in consequence of this very crime.
But even if no torment is sent on you in the world, how will you save yourselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. The Day which will make young children old (grey haired).

translation.text: the Day whose severity shall cause the heaven to split asunder? Allah's promise is ever bound to be fulfilled.
Surely this is a reminder. So let whoever wills take the ˹Right˺ Way to their Lord.

commentary.text: Whoever is desirous or interested then the “Right Path” is very clear and open. Welcome.

sections.title: 20 READ FROM THE QURAN AS MUCH AS YOU EASILY CAN AND..

translation.text: Surely your Lord knows that you ˹O Prophet˺ stand ˹in prayer˺ for nearly two-thirds of the night, or ˹sometimes˺ half of it, or a third, as do some of those with you. Allah ˹alone˺ keeps a ˹precise˺ measure of the day and night. He knows that you ˹believers˺ are unable to endure this and has turned to you in mercy. So recite ˹in prayer˺ whatever you can from the Quran. He knows that some of you will be sick, some will be travelling throughout the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and some fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite whatever you can from it. And ˹continue to˺ perform ˹regular˺ prayers, pay alms-tax, and lend to Allah a good loan. Whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with Allah far better and more rewarding. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: Ayat acknowledges the Prophet’s rigorous night worship—often extending to two-thirds, half, or a third of the night—and notes that a devoted group of companions emulated him. Allah SWT, who ordains the alternation of night and day, declares that precise calculation of these periods is difficult, and thus He mercifully abrogates the earlier obligation of prolonged night vigil. (This is the first part of the Ayat.)

Instead, believers are instructed to recite whatever portion of the Quran is manageable in tahajjud, given their varied conditions: illness, travel in pursuit of lawful provision, and striving in His cause. The Ayat then reaffirms obligatory duties—establishing prayer (5 times) and paying zakah—and enjoins voluntary charity as a “goodly loan” to Allah SWT, promising that every good deed sent ahead will be found with Him in superior and multiplied reward.
It concludes by commanding persistent istighfar, affirming Allah SWT’s enduring forgiveness and mercy.
Allah SWT says “easily” to show that worship is based on human capacity and divine mercy, so that devotion remains sincere, sustainable, and free from hardship rather than exhausting or overwhelming.
Dr Israr feels that when the 5 prayers were made obligatory the night prayres were nullified however in Ramadan is the time to renew our relationship with the Quran in night prayers and Tahajjud.

Allah SWT acknowledges the Prophet’s strenuous night worship and, knowing the community’s limitations and varying circumstances, lifts the earlier obligation of long tahajjud, permitting recitation of whatever is manageable. The Ayat reaffirms prayer, zakāh, voluntary charity with multiplied reward, and concludes by urging continual repentance to the Ever-Forgiving, Most-Merciful.
Lesson: Perform night prayers and read the Quran at night as much as you can. Allah SWT knows we cannot pray every night. The time of night changes every day so this too is a test.
Tahajud is not just a command for the Prophet (PBUH) rather it is for us too.
DEFINITION

arabic_lines: اَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ الۡقُرۡاٰنَ تَرۡتِيۡلً

translation.text: or a little more—and recite the Quran ˹properly˺ in a measured way.
translation.ref_as_written: restatement of 73:4 inside the 20-28 section (in-body summary unit)

commentary.text: TARTĪL means to recite the Qur’an slowly, clearly, and deliberately, giving each letter its proper articulation, observing tajwīd rules, and pausing thoughtfully so the meaning can be understood and reflected upon.

TAJWĪD literally means to make something excellent or precise. In Quranic recitation, it means pronouncing every letter correctly, from its proper articulation point (makhraj) and with its required characteristics (ṣifāt).
Why it matters:
Arabic letters are unforgiving. One tiny error can change the meaning completely. Tajwīd exists to prevent that disaster.

TAFSĪR means to explain, clarify, and uncover the intended meaning of the Qur’an. It deals with what Allah SWT means, not just what the words literally say. (i) Explanation of Ayats and vocabulary. (ii) Historical context (asbāb al-nuzūl). (iii)  Connections between Ayats and surahs. (iv) Legal, moral, and theological implications. (v) Clarifying what is general, specific, metaphorical, or literal.
TADABBUR means deep reflection and contemplation on the Quran. It is about thinking through the meanings, consequences, and personal implications of what Allah SWT is saying.
So tadabbur is not just reading the Ayat, but asking:
→ What does this lead to?
→ What does this require from me?
Relationship between the four:
Tajwīd: reciting correctly
Tartīl: reciting calmly and thoughtfully
Tafsīr: understanding the meaning
Tadabbur: letting that meaning sink in and reshape you
What is mentioned in Surah al-Muzzammil
Tartīl (73:4): reciting the Qur’an slowly and deliberately
Qiyām al-layl (73:2–6): standing in night prayer
Tabattul (73:8): complete devotion to Allah SWT
Nashi’at al-layl being ashaddu waṭ’an wa aqwamu qīlā (73:6): night worship being stronger in impact and more upright in speech.
All of these create the conditions for tadabbur.

items.text: The link between Surah al-Muzzammil (73) and Surah al-Muddaththir (74) is a deliberate progression from preparation to the commencement of the mission, from inner formation of strength to outward responsibility. Surah al-Muzzammil focuses on building the inner life of the Messenger (PBUH) through night prayer, Qur’anic recitation with tartīl, patience, trust in Allah SWT, and spiritual discipline. In its quiet, inward tone, the Prophet (PBUH) is trained in solitude, endurance, and deep intimacy with the Qur’an. This stage forms the strength, sincerity, and steadiness required to carry the weight of revelation.

Surah al-Muddaththir then breaks that stillness and shifts decisively outward. The command is no longer to stand in the night, but to rise and warn. The Prophet (PBUH) is called into public space, moral confrontation, rejection, and resistance. The surah exposes the arrogance of denial, the excuses of those who recognize truth yet refuse submission, and the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.

Together, the two surahs reveal a profound sequence. You cannot confront the world unless you have first conquered yourself. The night builds what the day will attempt to erode. Allah SWT, in His mercy, does not thrust His Messenger (PBUH) directly into hostility. He grants intimacy before responsibility, grounding before confrontation, and strength before strain.
This pattern is not unique to prophethood; it is a universal law for all who carry truth seriously. Without inner grounding, outward action becomes hollow, reactive, or self-serving.

The beauty of this pairing is not only structural or literary, but deeply humane. Allah SWT acknowledges human fragility and teaches the correct order of transformation be with Allah first, then stand before people. Once this link is seen, Surah al-Muzzammil and Surah al-Muddaththir no longer feel like separate chapters, but like one continuous movement of the soul, from silent formation to courageous proclamation.
Personal Statement: We have so many chances and choices in life. Sleep should not be one of them.
May this work be a hujja for me on the Day of Judgment in sha Allah.
Hadith: Al-Bukhari regarding Sahih al-Bukhari being a ḥujjah for him on the Day of Judgement.
Imam al-Bukhari is reported to have said words to this effect:
“I did not include in this book (al-Ṣaḥīḥ) any hadith except that it is authentic, and I did not include it until I prayed two rakʿahs and sought guidance from Allah.”
And in another wording attributed to him:
“I compiled the Ṣaḥīḥ from six hundred thousand hadiths, and I made it a proof (ḥujjah) between myself and Allah.”
MY KEY TAKEAWAYS
PROPHETS MISSION FOR INTERNAL STRENGTH
(73:2) Stand up in Prayer by night, all but a small part of it;
(73:3) ˹pray˺ half the night, or a little less,
(73:4) or a little more—and recite the Quran ˹properly˺ in a measured way.
(73:5) ˹For˺ We will soon send upon you a weighty revelation.
(73:6) Indeed, worship in the night is more impactful and suitable for recitation.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is named after the word occurring in its opening Ayat, al-muddaththir (“the one wrapped in his cloak”). As with many Makkan revelations, this functions as an identifying name rather than a thematic title.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
After the initial encounter in the Cave of Hira, revelation ceased for a period, leaving the Prophet in profound grief and spiritual anxiety.
During this interruption (fatrah al-waḥy), the Prophet (PBUH) would go to mountain peaks in a state of deep distress, contemplating the gravity of his experience. One day, after the period of silence, the Prophet (PBUH) heard a voice from the sky. Looking upward, he saw the same Angel he had encountered in Hira, now seated on a throne suspended between heaven and earth. Struck with fear, he hurried home and said, “Cover me, cover me.” His family wrapped him in a cloak, whereupon God revealed:
“O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn…”
This marked the renewal of revelation, which thereafter flowed with intensity and continuity.

front_matter.label: Theme & Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
SURAH AL-MUDDATHTHIR MARKS THE MOMENT WHEN THE PROPHET (PBUH)’S MISSION SHIFTS FROM INNER PREPARATION TO PUBLIC RESPONSIBILITY.
Prophet (PBUH) is given guidelines, duties, and mannerisms of being a Prophet.
After the initial revelation of Surah Al-‘Alaq and the subsequent pause that left him in deep spiritual anxiety, this Surah renews revelation with a decisive mandate: to arise, warn, magnify the Lord, purify both conduct and intention, sever attachment to worldly gain, and endure the hardships that would accompany proclamation. These opening Ayats define the foundational ethics of prophethood—sincerity, moral discipline, and steadfastness in the face of hostility.
Allah SWT calls the Prophet (PBUH) out of withdrawal and tells him to rise, warn, purify himself, glorify his Lord, abandon spiritual filth, and persevere for Allah alone. Surah al-Muddaththir teaches that once truth reaches you, neutrality is no longer an option. You either rise and respond, or you sink while making speeches about why you did not.
The surah then exposes what happens when people recognize truth but refuse responsibility. Arrogance, excuses, obsession with status, and denial of accountability lead straight to moral collapse and punishment. Salvation is shown to rest on personal responsibility, sincerity, and awareness of the Hereafter. No one is saved by lineage, intellect, or reputation. Each soul answers for itself.
The opening Ayats are a mission statement for Prophethood.
From Ayats 8–56 the Surah shifts warning, describing the certainty of judgment, the horror of Hell, and the fate of those who reject revelation despite inward awareness. It depicts the angels of punishment, the severity of Saqar, and the confession of its inhabitants—those who failed to pray, ignored the poor, indulged in frivolous discourse, and denied the Day of Reckoning.

sections.title: 1-7 INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PROPHET FOR CLEANLINESS AND PATIENCE

translation.text: O you covered up ˹in your clothes˺!

commentary.text: The background of the revelation of these Ayats as mentioned above can help one understand why the Prophet (PBUH) on this occasion has been addressed with Ya ayyuhal-Muddaththiru instead of Ya ayyuhar-Rasulu (O Messenger), or Ya ayyuhan-Nabiyyu (O Prophet).

The Prophet (PBUH) was terrified when he suddenly saw the Angel Gabriel, sitting on a throne between heaven and earth. He hastily home and asked the people of the house to cover him up, so Allah SWT addressed him with Ya ayyuhal-Muddaththiru. From this way of Allah SWT’s speech the meaning which automatically follows is: O My dear servant, why have you lain down thus enwrapped? You have been put under the burden of a great mission: you must now arise from your solitude to perform this mission with resolution and courage.

translation.text: Arise and warn ˹all˺.

commentary.text: A command of this very nature had been given to the prophet Nuh (PBUH) while appointing him to the office of Prophethood.
Surah Nuh Ayat 1
Warn the people of your nation before they are overtaken by a painful torment.

The Ayat means: ‘O you who lays enwrapped, stand up and arouse the people who live in heedlessness around you. Warn them of the fate which would certainly overtake them if they remained involved in the same heedlessness. Warn them that they are not living in a lawless kingdom where they are free to conduct themselves as they like and where they can do wherever they please without any fear or being called to account for it.’

translation.text: Revere your Lord ˹alone˺.

commentary.text: The passage teaches that the Prophet (PBUH)’s primary mission was to declare that true greatness belongs only to Allah SWT, refuting all false objects of reverence. This is why “Allahu Akbar” is central in Islamic worship and identity.

When this command was first revealed, the Prophet (PBUH) stood alone in Makkah—the center of Arabian idolatry. Declaring Allah’s Oneness in such an environment was dangerous. Therefore, the instruction to “Revere your Lord” also meant: Do not fear the forces around you; Allah SWT is greater than all who oppose you.

translation.text: Purify your garments.

commentary.text: The command “purify your garments” carries several layers of guidance.

First, it instructs the Prophet (PBUH) to maintain physical cleanliness, because purity of body and spirit are interconnected, and because he was tasked with teaching a society largely unfamiliar with concepts of cleanliness.
The Quran will be brought to the Prophet (PBUH) so he must maintain purity at every level.
Second, it calls for neatness and presentability, since a messenger of truth must not repel people through negligence in appearance.
Third, it forbids clothing that reflects arrogance, showiness, or vanity; a caller to Allah SWT must embody humility and dignity.
Fourth, it instructs moral purification, as “clean garments” in Arabic can also mean upright character and avoidance of dishonesty or blameworthy behavior.

translation.text: ˹Continue to˺ shun uncleanliness.

commentary.text: Un-cleanliness implies every kind of filth, whether of belief and thought, of morals and deeds, of the body, dress or mode of life. The Ayat means: Keep yourself free from the filth of evils which are prevalent in society around you: no one should ever impute to you the blame that your own life itself is stained in some degree with the evils that you tell others to avoid. So keep away from impure people or influences.

translation.text: Do not do a favour expecting more ˹in return˺.

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) is instructed to give purely for Allah SWT’s sake, without expecting any worldly return or increase. His knowledge, kindness, charity, and service must be free of self-interest. It also means he should not remind people of the immense favour they receive through his prophethood, nor seek any personal benefit from his mission.
وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ
And give not a thing (Tamnun) to have more.
Tamnun in the language of the Arabs means to become weak.
Lesson: Often what often holds us back from doing good is expectations of reward from man.  This brings disappointment and sadness. Expect reward only for Allah SWT and do only for Allah SWT.

translation.text: And persevere for ˹the sake of˺ your Lord.

commentary.text: This Ayat commands the Prophet (PBUH) to show steadfast, principled patience purely for the sake of Allah SWT. It prepares him for the reality that his mission will bring hostility, hardship, and opposition—even from his own people. He is instructed to remain firm, consistent in character, and unwavering in his mission, seeking no motive except his Lord’s pleasure.
Patience is being repeated in many of these Surahs.

These brief opening commands of prophethood perfectly outline what he must do, how he must live, and what trials he will face—evidence that these are divine instructions, not the product of human disorder or confusion.

commentary.text: Context of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah

Allah SWT commands the Prophet (PBUH) to leave the matter of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah entirely to Him. He was a powerful and influential leader of the Quraish. Allah SWT does not mention his name but via his attriutes we know who Allah SWT is talking about. Although Allah SWT created Walid as an only child, then gave him vast wealth, many sons (who were with him), social prestige, and made his life easy, Walid still demanded more and remained stubbornly arrogant and hostile to the revelation.

Although he privately recognized the Quran’s unmatched power. He admitted that Muhammad (PBUH) was neither mad, nor a poet, nor a soothsayer, nor a liar, and he openly praised the Quran as speech that was sweet, profound, and superior to all human composition. Because he began visiting the Prophet and Abu Bakr, the Quraysh feared he might accept Islam. Abu Jahl pressured him to publicly denounce the Prophet.

The Quran then describes how Walid schemed against the revelation. He thought, calculated, frowned, retreated, and finally arrogantly declared that the Quran was “ancient magic” and “the word of a human being.” For this deliberate slander, Allah SWT declares that he will be cast into Saqar—a hellfire that destroys completely, burns the skin, and is guarded by nineteen angels.

The Prophet (PBUH) is reassured that he does not need to concern himself with punishing or responding to this man—Allah Himself will take full charge of him. Allah SWT warns that Walid will face a harsh and unbearable punishment. (May Allah SWT save us of such a fate).
The passage captures this moment of deliberate denial, exposing his arrogance, ingratitude, and conscious rejection despite clear recognition of the truth. He was insistent on compromise.

items.text: The link between Surah al-Muzzammil (73) and Surah al-Muddaththir (74) is a deliberate progression from preparation to the commencement of the mission, from inner formation of strength to outward responsibility. Surah al-Muzzammil focuses on building the inner life of the Messenger (PBUH) through night prayer, Qur’anic recitation with tartīl, patience, trust in Allah SWT, and spiritual discipline. In its quiet, inward tone, the Prophet (PBUH) is trained in solitude, endurance, and deep intimacy with the Qur’an. This stage forms the strength, sincerity, and steadiness required to carry the weight of revelation.

Surah al-Muddaththir then breaks that stillness and shifts decisively outward. The command is no longer to stand in the night, but to rise and warn. The Prophet (PBUH) is called into public space, moral confrontation, rejection, and resistance. The surah exposes the arrogance of denial, the excuses of those who recognize truth yet refuse submission, and the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.

Together, the two surahs reveal a profound sequence. You cannot confront the world unless you have first conquered yourself. The night builds what the day will attempt to erode. Allah SWT, in His mercy, does not thrust His Messenger (PBUH) directly into hostility. He grants intimacy before responsibility, grounding before confrontation, and strength before strain.
This pattern is not unique to prophethood; it is a universal law for all who carry truth seriously. Without inner grounding, outward action becomes hollow, reactive, or self-serving.

The beauty of this pairing is not only structural or literary, but deeply humane. Allah SWT acknowledges human fragility and teaches the correct order of transformation be with Allah first, then stand before people. Once this link is seen, Surah al-Muzzammil and Surah al-Muddaththir no longer feel like separate chapters, but like one continuous movement of the soul, from silent formation to courageous proclamation.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Qiyāmah is named after its opening word and is fully devoted to the theme of Resurrection, making the name both a title and a thematic title.
Period of Revelation
Although no explicit tradition specifies the exact period of revelation, its content clearly indicates that it belongs to the early Meccan phase. The Surah reflects the early Quranic emphasis on affirming the Hereafter.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Qiyāmah belongs to the early Makkan period when revelation began to descend rapidly after the opening Ayats of Surah Al-Muddaththir. During this phase, the Quran presented its core beliefs and moral directives in brief, powerful statements or khutbas (speeches) that deeply unsettled the Quraysh leadership, compelling them to convene strategies to counter the Prophet (PBUH)’s message. This is an answer for those disbelievers who denied the DoJ.
This Surah addresses the deniers of the Resurrection, responding to their objections with firm reasoning. It establishes the possibility, inevitability, and necessity of the Hereafter, clarifying that denial is not rooted in intellectual doubt but in self-interest and resistance to moral accountability.
The Surah warns that the very event they reject will inevitably occur. On that Day, each person’s deeds will be fully exposed. Even before receiving his record, every individual will internally recognize the truth of his own actions, for no one is truly ignorant of what he has done—despite the excuses he may offer to others or to himself.
This is a pair with Surah Duha.

sections.title: 1-15 BE AWARE OF THE DAY OF RESURRECTION AND JUDGEMENT, THERE IS NO ESCAPE FROM IT

translation.text: Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection;

commentary.text: To begin the discourse with ‘Nay’ لَاۤ  by itself indicates that the Surah was sent down to refute some argument which was already in progress. This is also for further strengthening the oath.

The theme that follows shows that the argument was about Resurrection and life after death, which the people of Makkah were denying and mocking at it at the same time. Qiyaam means standing so the Day of Standing.

translation.text: And I do swear by the self-reproaching soul!

commentary.text: Again, Allah SWT says ‘Nay’ لَاۤ  to the false notion that the Day of Resurrection will never happen. In a scolding manner. Here Allah SWT swears by the self-reproaching soul (nafs al-lawwāmah), one of the three types of human souls or nafs or conscious mentioned in the Quran:
Ammārah – urges to evil Yusuf (12:53).

Lawwāmah – our conscious or Zameer that blames itself, feels guilt, recognizes right and wrong. Makes us feel bad at a mistake. Self-reproaching.  Our innate morality and sense of justice. (mentioned here)
Muṭma’innah – at peace with obedience Surah Al-Fajr (89:27).

By swearing an oath on the Resurrection and on the human conscience, Allah SWT is proving that life after death is certain. The self-reproaching soul shows humans are moral beings who expect justice. This moral demand cannot be fulfilled in the world alone, so it necessarily points to a Day of Judgment where every deed will be settled with perfect fairness.
Lesson: Humans know in their very fitra and soul that there will be a DoJ or a Day of Accounting however much they may try to suppress this truth.

translation.text: Do people think We cannot reassemble their bones?
Yes ˹indeed˺! We are ˹most˺ capable of restoring ˹even˺ their very fingertips.

commentary.text: Allah SWT can not only resurrect us but put our bones together to the point of even making our fingerprints exactly as they were in this world. Everyone has a unique fingerprint.

translation.text: Still people want to deny what is yet to come,

commentary.text: The real disease of the deniers of the Hereafter has been clearly diagnosed. What makes them deny the Hereafter is not, in fact, they’re regarding the Resurrection and Hereafter as impossible but they deny it because acceptance of the Hereafter inevitably imposes restrictions on them, which they detest.

They desire that they should have full freedom to go on committing whatever injustice, dishonesty, sin and wickedness that they have been committing before, and there should be no deterrent to obstruct their freedom and to warn them that one day they will have to appear and render an account of their deeds before their God.
Therefore, it is not their intellect which is hindering them from believing in the Hereafter but their desires of the self.

translation.text: asking ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”
But when the sight is stunned,

commentary.text: Man will be terror-stricken and amazed, and his eyes dazed and open in fright.

translation.text: and the moon is dimmed,
and the sun and the moon are brought together,
on that Day one will cry, “Where is the escape?”
But no! There will be no refuge.
On that Day all will end up before your Lord.
All will then be informed of what they have sent forth and left behind.

commentary.text: It means that on the Day of Judgment a person will be shown every deed, every neglect, and every consequence which will be fully laid out before him.
all the deeds and what he neglected to do,

Sadqa e jariaha, like useful knowledge, a well or a righteous child who prays for them. Or some bad inflences that are being passed down generation to generation. The lasting effects of those deeds that continued after his death, (his legacy where good or bad will also be attributed to him)
Lesson: Understand what legacy are you creating and leaving behind?

translation.text: In fact, people will testify against their own souls,

commentary.text: Man, himself will be a witness against himself.  Our tongues, our limbs and our body will testify to what we have done in this world.

translation.text: despite the excuses they come up with.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgment, a person’s record will be placed before him not to inform him of what he did, but to establish proof in the court of Allah SWT. Every person already knows the truth of his own actions, no matter how many excuses he invented in the world. A liar knows he lies, a wrongdoer knows exactly whom he harmed, and a corrupt person knows the truth behind every excuse he used to silence his conscience. So, when he stands before Allah SWT, he will already know why he is guilty, even while trying to defend himself.
Lesson: Today we commit atrocities, yet our bodies are loyal to us and we think our body is ours. But infact it is on loan to us from Allah SWT.

sections.title: 16-30 ALLAH HIMSELF TOOK THE RESPONSIBILITY OF AL-QURAN AND LAST MOMENTS OF DISBELIEVER'S DEATH

translation.text: Do not rush your tongue trying to memorize ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran.
It is certainly upon Us to ˹make you˺ memorize and recite it.
So once We have recited a revelation ˹through Gabriel˺, follow its recitation ˹closely˺.

commentary.text: This Ayat interrupts the flow to address the Prophet (PBUH) directly. In the early days of revelation, he would repeat the Quran quickly while Jibreel recited, afraid he might forget any part of it. Allah SWT reassured the Prophet (PBUH): ‘do not rush your tongue, simply listen; We will make you remember it perfectly and recite it accurately.’ Thus, do not compromise of listening and place your trust in Allah SWT.
Lesson: When learning anything but especially the Quran do not multitask and stay focused.

translation.text: Then it is surely upon Us to make it clear ˹to you˺.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is telling the Prophet (PBUH) that He Himself will explain the Quran’s meanings to him. This means: The Prophet didn’t receive only the words of the Quran; he also received their meanings and explanations through revelation.

As well as the order of the Ayats known as tarteeb-e-Mushaf. At the time of wahi it was also revealed where to place the Ayats in the Quran. So, the order is divine and not man-made. The Ayats were placed exactly where the Prophet (PBUH) was told to place them, and the surahs were arranged under his direction before he died. The companions wrote it down and preserved it exactly as he recited it.
Angel Gibraeil heard the Quran in its complete order twice during the Prophet (PBUH) last Ramadan.

Therefore, the Sunnah and Hadith carry legal and interpretive authority, because they are the Prophet’s divinely taught explanation of the Quran. Without this explanation, no one could know details of commands like salah, zakat, hajj, etc., from the Quran alone.

translation.text: But no! In fact, you love this fleeting world,

commentary.text: After giving this instruction, the Surah returns to its main theme.
The address is to the disbelievers.

‘Nay’ لَاۤ  implies: You deny the Hereafter not because you regard the Creator of the universe as helpless to bring about Resurrection and raise the dead, rather because you love the world with all its glamor and distractions.

translation.text: and neglect the Hereafter.

commentary.text: We become heedless of the Hereafter. When making decisions we go for this world and not the Hereafter. Often compromising our Hereafter.

translation.text: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright,

commentary.text: On the DoJ some faces will be glowing, full of light (nur) and radiant.

translation.text: looking at their Lord.

commentary.text: They will be looking towards their Raab and will see their Raab. This is what they longed for in this world.

translation.text: And ˹other˺ faces will be gloomy,

commentary.text: While other faces will be distorted, distressed and frowning.

translation.text: anticipating something devastating to befall them.

commentary.text: This is because they know what and where their outcome will be. They know something bad will happen very soon.
FYI – They will not be allowed to see Allah SWT. Allah wants nothing to do with them.

translation.text: But no! ˹Beware of the day˺ when the soul reaches the collar bone ˹as it leaves˺,

commentary.text: ‘Nay’ لَاۤ  . Beware of the day when the death rattle or soul reaches the collar bone. Limbs become lifeless and cold but the person is still breathing.

translation.text: and it will be said, “Is there any healer ˹who can save this life˺?”

commentary.text: When a person is on the brink of death and all treatments fail, the people around him say, “Is there any raqī — anyone who can help now?” The word raqīn/raqī can mean two things:
From “ruqyah”: People desperately call for someone to perform spiritual healing or chanting when they’ve run out of options.
From “raqi” (ascending): It refers to the angels deciding who will take the soul — the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment.
So the Ayat captures that final, helpless moment when neither medicine nor magic nor excuses matter anymore; the soul is being claimed, and its fate is decided right then.

translation.text: And the dying person realizes it is ˹their˺ time to depart,

commentary.text: The dying person knows that the departing time as come. No more life in the legs is left.

translation.text: and ˹then˺ their feet are tied together ˹in a shroud˺.

commentary.text: Death first happens from the feet then moves up.

translation.text: On that day they will be driven to your Lord ˹alone˺.

commentary.text: The procession to the Lord begins.

sections.title: 31-40 DISBELIEVERS DO NOT BELIEVE BECAUSE THEY NEVER TOOK AL-ISLAM SERIOUSLY

translation.text: This denier neither believed nor prayed,
but persisted in denial and turned away,
then went to their own people, walking boastfully.

commentary.text: The Ayat describes a man who heard the warnings of Surah Al-Qiyāmah, knew exactly what they meant, and still walked right back to his people swaggering with arrogance. Early commentators say this was Abu Jahl, which fits the vibe perfectly.

The Quran points out that he refused to accept the truth and refused to pray, which exposes the real problem: his denial wasn’t intellectual, it was pride. If someone truly accepts God and His Messenger, the very first visible sign is salah, because its obligation comes immediately after faith.

translation.text: Woe to you, and more woe!
Again, woe to you, and even more woe!

commentary.text: This is a cutting, sarcastic rebuke. It means something like: “This is exactly what suits someone like you.”

Since this person arrogantly denied his Creator, then this disgrace and doom are perfectly fitting for him. It’s the same sharp tone used elsewhere in the Quran, like telling a criminal in Hell: “Taste this, you mighty, honorable man.”
Your fate matches your arrogance.
May Allah SWT save us from such a horrible fate. Ameen.

translation.text: Do people think they will be left without purpose?

commentary.text: Now, in conclusion, the same theme is being repeated with which the discourse began life-after-death is necessary as well as possible.
Does man think that he has been brought here to earth and given this life at random. This is not a question rather a point to contemplate and reflect upon.

translation.text: Were they not ˹once˺ a sperm-drop emitted?
Then they became a clinging clot ˹of blood˺, then He developed and perfected their form,
producing from it both sexes, male and female.
Is such ˹a Creator˺ unable to bring the dead back to life?

commentary.text: The One who created a human being from a tiny drop of fluid clearly has the power to bring him back to life after death. Anyone who admits creation is purposeful cannot deny resurrection.
Even those who claim everything is “accident” have no explanation for the precise, balanced continuation of humans across all ages and nations.
Lesson: So this life is for a purpose – which is to worship our Raab. Death is certain!!
Soon we will be taking our last and final breath.
Prepare of the end journey NOW!!
