titles: 1-12 UNIVERSE WAS THERE BEFORE MANKIND, THEN ALLAH CREATED MAN, PROVIDED HIM GUIDANCE AND LET HIM USE HIS FREE WILL, EITHER TO BELIEVE OR TO DISBELIEVE
13-22 EXEMPLARY LIFE IN PARADISE FOR THOSE WHO CHOOSE TO BELIEVE
23-31 ALLAH SENT THIS QURAN GRADUALLY ACCORDING TO THE ISSUES FACED BY MANKIND AND THIS IS AND ADMONITION FOR THOSE WHO WANT TO ADOPT THE WAY TO THEIR RABB (GOD)

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of this Surah is in the first Ayat. This Surah is called Ad-Dahr and Al-Insān.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Most major scholars say it is Makki, and its style clearly matches the early Makkan revelations.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah reminds humans of their humble beginning, when they were nothing, and shows how Allah SWT created them, gave them intelligence, and showed them the path of gratitude and the path of disbelief. Life is a test: the grateful servant meets a blessed end, and the ungrateful meets a terrible one.
Ayat 5–22 describe in vivid detail the rewards prepared for those who live with sincerity, patience, and righteousness.
The Surah closes by exposing the real cause of disbelief: obsession with the world and forgetfulness of the Hereafter. Allah SWT reminds humans that He created them, can replace them, can revive them, and will judge them.

sections.title: 1-12 UNIVERSE WAS THERE BEFORE MANKIND, THEN ALLAH CREATED MAN, PROVIDED HIM GUIDANCE AND LET HIM USE HIS FREE WILL, EITHER TO BELIEVE OR TO DISBELIEVE

translation.text: Is there not a period of time when each human is nothing yet worth mentioning?

commentary.text: This Surah begins from the end of Surah 75. That is man was created from a sperm drop.

The Ayat uses a rhetorical question to remind humans that there was indeed a time in the vast span of existence when the human species did not exist, and when everyone was nothing more than unformed microscopic material, unknown and unnoticed.
The point is to make the listener reflect that the One who brought humans from such an insignificant, hidden beginning to full creation is fully able to create them again after death.
Saira was not in existence before July 1st 1966.

translation.text: ˹For˺ indeed, We ˹alone˺ created humans from a drop of mixed fluids, ˹in order˺ to test them, so We made them hear and see.

commentary.text: God created the human being from a mixed drop, meaning the fused sperm and ovum. This humble origin is tied to the purpose of life: THE HUMAN IS PLACED ON EARTH TO BE TESTED BUT TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE. For that test, God granted him hearing and sight, meaning the intellectual and perceptive faculties through which he gains knowledge, forms judgments, and becomes morally responsible.

arabic_lines: اِنَّا هَدَيۡنٰهُ السَّبِيۡلَ اِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَّاِمَّا كَفُوۡرًا

translation.text: We already showed them the Way, whether they ˹choose to˺ be grateful or ungrateful.

commentary.text: Allah SWT made guidance accessible to the human being after granting him reason and perception. This guidance appears in many forms: (i) an innate moral sense that distinguishes good and evil, (ii) the conscience that rebukes wrongdoing, (iii) the signs of God within the human self and throughout the universe, human experiences that point to a higher power, and the (iv) universal intuition that justice requires reward and punishment.
So not only does man have physical eyes but also an innate sense to distinguish good from bad. Then Allah SWT below into man His ruh/spirit. Then gave man freedom to choose.
To complete this guidance, Allah SWT also sent prophets and revealed scriptures to clarify the path of gratitude (faith and obedience) and the path of ingratitude (disbelief and disobedience).

Lesson: Man is created for a very short time. THIS IS MT TIME ON EARTH maybe 80 years. Soon I will be gone and my test complete. With every test Allah SWT test or see how I respond that is if I am grateful or if I deny/am a kafir.
The way a person lives in this life he will see in the Hereafter.
After receiving all these means/agencies, a person’s choice is entirely his own responsibility.

translation.text: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a blazing Fire.
Indeed, the virtuous will have a drink ˹of pure wine˺—flavoured with camphor—
˹from˺ a spring where Allah’s servants will drink, flowing at their will.

commentary.text: The servants of Allah SWT will make the springs gush themselves at their will.
Lesson: In this world the servants of Allah SWT submitted/were subservient to Allah SWT laws and commands. So, in the next the reward is much more autonomy.

translation.text: They ˹are those who˺ fulfil ˹their˺ vows and fear a Day of sweeping horror,

commentary.text: Righteous believers who faithfully carry out the obligations Allah SWT has placed on them often coupled with voluntary acts. They set high standards for themselves.
They fear of the Day of Judgment.

translation.text: and give food—despite their desire for it—to the poor, the orphan, and the captive,

commentary.text: Sincerity of the righteous: when they give to those in need, they do it purely for Allah SWT’s pleasure, not seeking praise, repayment, or gratitude.
Mentioning feeding the poor is simply an example; all forms of relieving hardship are included. They help and give without being stingy or small hearted.
Lesson: Spend out of what you love not necessarily what you have.

arabic_lines: اِنَّمَا نُطۡعِمُكُمۡ لِـوَجۡهِ اللّٰهِ لَا نُرِيۡدُ مِنۡكُمۡ جَزَآءً وَّلَا شُكُوۡرًا

translation.text: ˹saying to themselves,˺ “We feed you only for the sake of Allah, seeking neither reward nor thanks from you.

commentary.text: Hoping for the reward of Allah SWT and His pleasure and not from man. This is a man who crushes his own ego or desires to boost in front of others. To see the face of Allah SWT. They want nothing from people only from Allah SWT.

translation.text: We fear from our Lord a horribly distressful Day.”
So Allah will deliver them from the horror of that Day, and grant them radiance and joy,

commentary.text: Radiance and joy: radiance of the face and joy of the heart. In other words, all the severities and terrors of the Day of Resurrection will be meant only for the disbelievers and the culprits.
The righteous will on that Day remain immune from every hardship and will be well pleased with their lot.
Lesson: You bring happiness to others, i.e. by feeding and helping them and Allah SWT will bring joy and radiance to you in sha Allah.

translation.text: and reward them for their perseverance with a Garden ˹in Paradise˺ and ˹garments of˺ silk.

commentary.text: Reward for the sabr/patience and steadfastness the righteous is paradise.

A believer’s life is full of patience. Iman has two wings (i) Sabr and (ii) Sukur. A believer is either in a state of gratitude (in good times) or patience (in times of difficulty). Controlling, being steadfast thus not in a state of denial or kufur.
So, in this world the believer is always in an active state of patience, steadfastness and sabr and striving. This is exhausting and hard work. Below is the reward in Heaven.

translation.text: There they will be reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches, never seeing scorching heat or bitter cold.

commentary.text: Life was not easy. But now the people of paradise can relax, recline and chill on comfy couches. In shade and privacy in the perfect temperature, nothing extreme.

translation.text: The Garden’s shade will be right above them, and its fruit will be made very easy to reach.
They will be waited on with silver vessels and cups of crystal—
crystalline silver, filled precisely as desired.
And they will be given a drink ˹of pure wine˺ flavoured with ginger
from a spring there, called Salsabîl.
They will be waited on by eternal youths. If you saw them, you would think they were scattered pearls.
And if you looked around, you would see ˹indescribable˺ bliss and a vast kingdom.
The virtuous will be ˹dressed˺ in garments of fine green silk and rich brocade, and adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ هٰذَا كَانَ لَـكُمۡ جَزَآءً وَّكَانَ سَعۡيُكُمۡ مَّشۡكُوۡرً

translation.text: ˹And they will be told,˺ “All this is surely a reward for you. Your striving has been appreciated.”

commentary.text: This reward is not just for what you have achieved but for your striving or effort. Your saee. Your endeavors have been accepted and recognized, and Allah SWT appreciates your life’s works, objectives energies and abilities. Thus, here is the reward!

Hadith: Allah SWT will say to the last person to be admitted into Heaven that he will have everything equal to the earth and ten times more. When the Angels saw Heaven they said it is a home for kings.

Lesson: If we want a place in paradise, we cannot be lazy. Saee in Haj or Umarah it tough that is walking and for men sometimes running up and down. Similarly in this world we must work hard and strive for Heaven. Say your salah five times a day every day. Zikr AM and PM. Do good deeds and continue to restore your Iman every day.

translation.text: Indeed, it is We Who have revealed the Quran to you ˹O Prophet˺ in stages.

commentary.text: Allah SWT declares that He Himself revealed the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH) in gradual stages or portions thus the Ayat affirms that the gradual revelation was a deliberate act of divine wisdom, not human composition.
Gradual revelation to strengthen the heart of the Prophet (PBUH), easy to remember and internalize, at times revelation came due to a certain situation or context.
This is also a response to the unbelievers’ claim that the Prophet (PBUH) authored the Quran piece by piece.

arabic_lines: فَاصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعۡ مِنۡهُمۡ اٰثِمًا اَوۡ كَفُوۡرًاۚ

translation.text: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not yield to any evildoer or ˹staunch˺ disbeliever from among them.

commentary.text: “Be patient”: O Prophet (PBUH) face patiently the hardships and difficulties of the great Mission your Lord has entrusted to upon you.

“Do not yield or obey”: Do not yield to any one so as to give up preaching of the true faith; do not be inclined to make even the least change in the religious beliefs for the sake of any denier of the truth.
Openly assert/declare whatever is unlawful and forbidden and whatever is true as true and do not adopt even a little leniency in this regard.

translation.text: ˹Always˺ remember the Name of your Lord morning and evening,

commentary.text: At the beginning of the day and at its end. Zikr AM and PM.

translation.text: and prostrate before Him during part of the night, and glorify Him long at night.

commentary.text: Prostrate before God and glorify Him during the extended hours of the night. This includes the obligatory night prayers (Maghrib and Isha) and especially the late-night Tahajjud, which strengthens patience, spiritual resilience, and readiness to face opposition.
The Quran consistently links steadfastness against disbelief with abundant remembrance of God and regular prayer.
FYI – This is early Makkan Surah when 5 prayers were not mandated. So, night prayer was stressed.

translation.text: Surely those ˹pagans˺ love this fleeting world, ˹totally˺ neglecting a weighty Day ahead of them.

commentary.text: The reason why the disbelieving Quraish still persist in the errors and deviations of belief and why they turn a deaf ear to the Prophets (PBUH) invitation to the truth is, in fact, their worship of the world and their heedlessness of the Hereafter.

translation.text: It is We Who created them and perfected their ˹physical˺ form. But if We will, We can easily replace them with others.

commentary.text: Allah SWT created us and firmly shaped our physical structure. Because He is our Maker, He also has full power to change or replace us whenever He wills. This includes removing one community and bringing another in its place, altering a person’s condition in this life, or resurrecting them in a new form after death.
Lesson: Our bodies and limbs were created as such so that we can worship Allah SWT. Do ruku and sujood and recite and understand the Quran.

translation.text: Surely this is a reminder. So let whoever wills take the ˹Right˺ Way to their Lord.

commentary.text: The Quran is a Reminder, and Guidance from Allah SWT. But important to remember that even if a person asks for guidance, it will only come if Allah SWT wishes.

translation.text: But you cannot will ˹to do so˺ unless Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

commentary.text: A person may choose the path he wishes, but his choice cannot take effect unless God allows it. Human freedom operates within the limits of God’s supreme will, and nothing can be accomplished without His permission. Yet God’s will is never arbitrary: He acts with complete knowledge and wisdom, granting or withholding outcomes according to what He knows each person deserves.
Lesson: Don’t become proud when you are doing a good deed because that too is only by the permission of Allah SWT. It is infact our good fortune.

translation.text: He admits whoever He wills into His mercy. As for the wrongdoers, He has prepared for them a painful punishment

commentary.text: Allah SWT grants entry into His mercy to whomever He wills, and those He admits are those who accept His guidance and follow the revelation.
As for the wrongdoers—those who knowingly reject His message or claim to believe while refusing to obey—they have a severe punishment prepared for them.
Guidance and misguidance both occur by the will of Allah SWT, and no one can guide the one Allah SWT allows to stray or mislead the one Allah SWT chooses to guide.
Lesson: Our intentions guide our actions, but Allah SWT is the One who allows us to take the actions.

29-40 ON THAT DAY, THE DISBELIEVERS WILL BE ASKED TO WALK TOWARDS HELL WHICH THEY USED TO DENY
41-45 THE RIGHTEOUS WILL BE GIVEN ALL THAT THEY DESIRE

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This Surah was revealed in the earliest period at Makkah. If this Surah is read together with the two Surahs preceding it, namely Al-Qiyamah and Ad-Dahr, and the two Surahs following it, namely An-Naba and An-Naziat, it becomes obvious that all these Surahs were revealed at the same period, and they deal with the same theme.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text: The Surah establishes the certainty of Resurrection and the Hereafter. It warns those who mock the Hereafter and describes the punishment awaiting them, while promising reward for those who believe and live righteously. It ends by declaring that anyone who fails to take guidance from the Quran has no other source of true guidance.

sections.title: 1-28 ALLAH SWEARS IN THE NAME OF LIFE GIVING WINDS, RAIN AND ANGELS THAT THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT WILL BE ESTABLISHED AND WOE ON THAT DAY TO THE DISBELIEVERS!

translation.text: By the (winds) sent forth in quick succession,

commentary.text: Allah SWT's is swearing or taking an oath by the winds (that bring/or send forth clouds and rain) and angels (who carry out Allah SWT commands) about the Certainty of the Occurrence of the Hereafter.
Both winds and angels (Ayat 4) are invisible and intangible like the DoJ. Both bring mercy and punishment.
Name of Surah.

translation.text: and those blowing violently,
and those scattering ˹rainclouds˺ widely!

commentary.text: Winds that bring rain and clouds. Both gentle and violent.

translation.text: And ˹by˺ those ˹angels˺ fully distinguishing ˹truth from falsehood˺,

commentary.text: The angels who, by Allah SWT’s command, separate and clarify revelation with precision, just as winds separate and disperse clouds, highlighting that divine guidance decisively distinguishes right from wrong and leaves humanity without confusion before the coming judgment.

translation.text: and those delivering revelation,

commentary.text: The angels who faithfully convey Allah SWT’s message to His Messengers, just as the winds carry clouds by Divine command; the oath emphasizes that revelation, like the natural order, operates under precise authority and purpose, reinforcing the certainty of accountability and the Hereafter.

translation.text: ending excuses and giving warnings.

commentary.text: The ordered system of winds and rain serves as both mercy and warning, awakening hearts to the power of Allah SWT and proving that the One who sustains and regulates the universe with precise law can just as easily end it and recreate it for the sake of perfect justice in the Hereafter.

The winds are presented as a sign that stirs people into remembering Allah SWT. Their pattern— of raising clouds, spreading them, and bringing rain—shows deliberate design, not chance. This purposeful system proves both the possibility and the necessity of the Resurrection: The One Who sustains life through such ordered forces can certainly recreate mankind, and His justice requires a final judgment where every deed is fully rewarded or punished.
Thus, the winds serve as reminders that a Day of Resurrection is real, inevitable, and affirmed by revelation.

translation.text: Surely, what you are promised will come to pass.

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears an oath that what people are promised—Resurrection and the Hereafter—is certain to occur. The oath is taken by the winds in their various states: blowing in succession, violently, dispersing, separating clouds, and stirring remembrance in human hearts. These observable patterns in the winds show the power and wisdom of Allah SWT, proving both the possibility and inevitability of the Resurrection, and that the One Who controls such forces can easily bring life, end it, and recreate it.
Below is the description of the DoJ

translation.text: So when the stars are put out,
and the sky is torn apart,
and the mountains are blown away,
and the messengers’ time ˹to testify˺ comes up—
for which Day has all this been set?
To the Day of Judgement.
And what will make you realize what the Day of Decision is?
Woe on that Day to the deniers!

commentary.text: Deniers: those people who took the news of the coming of Resurrection as a lie and spent their lives in the world under the delusion that the time would never come when they would have to present themselves before their God and render an account of their deeds.
This phrase will come 10 times in this Surah

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
Did We not create you from a humble fluid,
placing it in a secure place

commentary.text: Placing the baby securing in its mother womb.

translation.text: until an appointed time?

commentary.text: For about nine months.

translation.text: We ˹perfectly˺ ordained ˹its development˺. How excellent are We in doing so!

commentary.text: Allah SWT decrees everything for the baby, i.e., male/female etc.

Additionally, this is an assertion for life-after-death that is, when Allah SWT had the power to shape and develop you into a perfect and complete man from an insignificant sperm-drop, then Allah SWT can re-create/resurrect you as well.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
Have We not made the earth a container
for the living and the dead,

commentary.text: The earth sustains those who are alive and keeps those who are dead.
Lesson: When we make things that are not sustainable or biodegradable, i.e., plastic straws etc., we are going against nature.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!

commentary.text: Woe to the deniers who are witnessing all the signs, blessings and miracles around you still deny.

sections.title: 29-40 ON THAT DAY, THE DISBELIEVERS WILL BE ASKED TO WALK TOWARDS HELL WHICH THEY USED TO DENY

translation.text: ˹The disbelievers will be told,˺ “Proceed into that ˹Fire˺ which you used to deny!

commentary.text: Now Allah SWT tells us how the deniers will be dealt with on the DoJ -- which will certainly occur.

translation.text: Proceed into the shade ˹of smoke˺ which rises in three columns,

commentary.text: Shadow of smoke; three columns: Because when a big smoke arises, it is divided into several parts at the top.

translation.text: Providing neither coolness nor shelter from the flames.

commentary.text: The shade of the smoke that comes from the flame -- which itself will not have a shade, nor will it benefit against the flame. It will not protect them from the heat of the flame.

translation.text: Indeed, it hurls sparks ˹as big˺ as huge castles,
and ˹as dark˺ as black camels.”
Woe on that Day to the deniers!
On that Day they will not ˹be in a position to˺ speak,

commentary.text: The deniers will not be albe to speak out of fear and awe.
Lesson: On this earth they spoke a lot, argued, mocked. Said that when they die they will argue with Allah SWT or give their point of view. May Allah SWT save us from such arrogance.

translation.text: nor will they be permitted to offer excuses.

commentary.text: They will be offering all sorts of excuses, blaming others for their errors and proving their own selves to be innocent, abusing their leaders and guides who led them astray; so much so that some of them will even disown their crimes shamelessly, as has been stated at several places in the Quran.

But when their being criminals will have been established by every kind of evidence, and when their own hands and feet and limbs will have borne witness against them to prove their guilt fully, and when after fulfilling all requirements of justice rightly and truly, the sentence will be passed on them, they will be dumbfounded and no room will be left for them to offer any excuse.
Their guilt and crime will be proved to the fullest and they will not be able to offer any excuse after it.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
˹They will be told by Allah,˺ “This is the Day of ˹Final˺ Decision: We have gathered you along with earlier disbelievers ˹for punishment˺.
So if you have a scheme ˹to save yourselves˺, then use it against Me.”

commentary.text: That is, in the world you used every kind of deception and trick in self-interest. Now, if you have any trick to escape My punishment, you may use it to defeat Me and My plan.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!

sections.title: 41-45 THE RIGHTEOUS WILL BE GIVEN ALL THAT THEY DESIRE

translation.text: Indeed, the righteous will be amid ˹cool˺ shade and springs
and any fruit they desire.
˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink happily for what you used to do.”
Surely this is how We reward the good-doers.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS

sections.title: 45 – 50 WOE TO THE DENIERS

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
“Eat and enjoy yourselves for a little while, ˹for˺ you are truly wicked.”

commentary.text: In conclusion, these words are being addressed not only to the disbelievers of Makkah but to all disbelievers of the world. This life is a place of very brief enjoyment.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
When it is said to them, “Bow down ˹before Allah,” they do not bow.

commentary.text: Bowing before Allah SWT: does not only imply worshipping Him but also means believing in Allah SWT’s Messenger (PBUH) and in the Book revealed by Him and following and obeying His commands. They would turn away arrogantly.
So for those who do not bow or do sajuood in this world when they are told to bow on the DoJ they will not be able to do so.
Those who deny will not be able to do the most honorable thing that is do ruku and sujood. They rejected and enjoyed life and Allah SWt’s blessings.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
So what message after this ˹Quran˺ would they believe in?

commentary.text: Lesson: Accept before it is too late. Obey/submit/Believe.

items.text: وَيْلٌ   يَوْمَئِذٍ   لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
(77:49) Woe on that Day to the deniers!
WOE TO THE DENIERS WHO ARE WITNESSING ALL THE SIGNS, BLESSINGS AND MIRACLES AROUND YOU STILL DENY.
This statement by Allah SWT has been mentioned 10 times in the Surah. Preceding this are clear evidence, whether signs in creation, the fate of past nations, or scenes of the Day of Judgment.

After every proof, the same declaration returns: “Woe on that Day to the deniers,” functioning like a judicial verdict that seals the argument. The repetition intensifies the warning, reinforces the certainty of accountability before Allah SWT, and underscores that persistent denial, despite clear signs, carries inevitable consequences.
So bow down, submit and obey.
